title: Detectors: tape speed, imbalance, regime, iceberg/stop-run (estimated)
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 6, sprints S10-S13, version `0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E25 Detectors** is the *interpretation* layer of that release: it turns the raw tape and the reconstructed L2 book into a small number of named, tunable, explainable signals - speed of tape, book speed, imbalance stacks, absorption, iceberg, stop-run and market regime.

Roadmap scope line (section 6.2): "Speed-of-tape (trades/sec, volume/sec, with baseline z-score); imbalance tracker with stacked-imbalance runs; market-regime classifier (trend / balance / volatile) from range, volume and delta features; **iceberg detector (estimated)** - repeated refills at a price level beyond visible depth; **stop-run detector (estimated)** - sweep beyond a swing level followed by rapid reversion; every detector exposes its inputs and thresholds in an inspector so the user can see *why* it fired" - **34 pts, S12-S13**, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`server/orderflow/`), story domain **DET** (9 stories: 6 Must, 3 Should).

Two invariants govern the whole epic:

1. **Honesty (R2 exit criterion #4).** Bybit publishes no L3/MBO data. Iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences over anonymous aggregated public data. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` states: `confidence="estimated"` is mandatory for every heuristic, and "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface in this epic therefore carries CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the methodology drawer. A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic.
2. **Single-source evaluation (R2 exit criteria #1 and #7).** Detectors are computed once, backend-side, in M9, published on the single WS topic `metrics.{symbol}` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`: "Derived order-flow series share one topic ... They are one engine output family and one subscription, not five"), persisted to QuestDB `orderflow_metrics`, and consumed identically by the panels, the alert engine, the rule DSL (E35) and the journal. A second client-side implementation of any threshold is an explicit anti-goal. Detector outputs must be reproducible: replaying the same recorded window twice yields identical events (exit criterion #7).

## Goal
Ship every DET user story that belongs to R2, backend-first, so that a trader can see *what* the market is doing (speed, imbalance, regime) and *why the terminal thinks so* (inputs, thresholds, failure modes), with every heuristic honestly labelled and every threshold auditable - because detector output can feed armed rules that place real orders.

## Scope / Deliverables
User stories: **US-DET-001** Speed of tape (Must), **US-DET-002** Tape acceleration and threshold alerts (Should), **US-DET-003** Book speed (Should), **US-DET-004** Imbalance tracker panel (Must), **US-DET-005** Absorption detector (Must), **US-DET-006** Iceberg / hidden-order detector (Should), **US-DET-007** Stop-run / liquidity sweep detector (Must), **US-DET-008** Market regime classifier (Must), **US-DET-009** Detector configuration and audit of estimates (Must).

Screens: **SCR-055** Speed-of-tape panel; **SCR-056** Imbalance tracker panel; **SCR-057** Market regime panel; **SCR-058** Detector methodology drawer ("Why estimated?"); **SCR-059** Detector settings dialog. (SCR-104 Scanner consumes the `trades_per_sec` metric but is owned by E17.)

Components: CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge, CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane, CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator, CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip, CMP-134 DetectorEventCard, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-049 Table, CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-021 Link, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-010 Slider, CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-026 EmptyState.

Backend (module M9, `server/orderflow/`): `MetricsEngine` (rolling tape/book statistics and z-scores), `DetectorRegistry` + `DetectorEvent` bus, `AbsorptionDetector`, `IcebergDetector`, `StopRunDetector`, `ImbalanceStackTracker`, `RegimeClassifier`.
API: `GET /api/v1/market/metrics`, `GET|PUT /api/v1/detectors/config`, `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology`, `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain`.
WS: `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics[]` selecting `trades_per_sec`, `volume_per_sec`, `book_updates_per_sec`, `tape_acceleration`, `imbalance_ratio`, `absorption`, `iceberg`, `stop_run`, `adx`, `atr`, `hurst`, `regime`.
DB: QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` (`trades_per_sec`, `notional_per_sec`, `book_imbalance`, `book_thickness`, `realized_vol_1m`, `atr_14`, `regime`, `regime_confidence`, `stacked_imbalance_up`, `stacked_imbalance_down`, `iceberg_score`, `stoprun_score`, `absorption_score`); Postgres detector-config rows (global plus per-symbol override) and the append-only audit log.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell aggregation and the imbalance *ratio* computation itself (E18 - this epic consumes footprint imbalance flags and only tracks *stacks* over time).
- DOM ladder, heatmap and L2 book reconstruction (E21 - consumed as an input).
- CVD/delta series (E23 - consumed as a regime sub-signal).
- Big-trade thresholds and bubbles (E22).
- Alert delivery, cooldown scheduling and the alert centre (ALRT domain - this epic only emits detector events onto the shared event bus; US-DET-002's alert UI lives there).
- Rule DSL vocabulary binding and evaluation (E35) - this epic guarantees the metric codes exist and are documented.
- Replay clock and scrubbing (E26 owns the clock; this epic must simply be clock-agnostic).
- Scanner/screener columns (E17) and journal auto-tagging.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One family, one subscription
  Given a client subscribes to metrics.BTCUSDT with metrics ["trades_per_sec","regime","iceberg","stop_run"]
  Then all four series arrive on that single subscription
  And no separate tapespeed, regime or detector topic exists

Scenario: Honesty gate
  Given any detector-derived value is rendered anywhere in the app
  Then it carries the (estimated) badge wherever the metric vocabulary marks the metric estimated
  And activating the badge opens SCR-058 at that detector's section

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the same recorded window is replayed twice
  Then the emitted detector event streams are identical

Scenario: Missing dependency
  Given a symbol has no recorded L2 history
  Then the iceberg and stop-run detectors are shown disabled, naming the missing dependency, with a one-click start-recording action

Scenario: Auditability
  When a detector threshold is changed
  Then an append-only audit record is written with detector, key, before, after and actor
```

## Exit criteria
1. All nine DET stories accepted; every Must story demonstrable on a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day and live on demo.
2. Every estimated surface carries CMP-227 with a working link to SCR-058, and SCR-058 contains a section per estimated signal stating what it infers, from what data, with which thresholds in force, and its known false-positive modes (R2 exit criterion #4).
3. Determinism: replaying an identical recorded window twice produces identical detector event streams (R2 exit criterion #7), enforced by a CI golden-fixture test.
4. Detectors are computed only backend-side; no threshold logic exists in the web client (review plus a lint rule on the panels package).
5. `metrics.{symbol}` carries the whole family in one subscription; WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms holds with the detector metric set added (budget #3, hard R2 gate).
6. Every detector threshold change is audited, and the settings dialog warns when armed rules depend on the detector being changed.
7. Detectors degrade explicitly on missing dependencies, never to a silent zero.
8. a11y pass on SCR-055..059 (WCAG 2.2 AA): text-first values, no colour-only encodings, keyboard-navigable event lists.
9. Coverage floors held (backend/engine >=85 %, frontend >=80 %); zero open P0/P1; QA sign-off; design sign-off on all five screens.

## Risks
| Risk | Why | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| R7 Data accuracy | Iceberg/stop-run/absorption are inferences over L2-only data; a false positive that feeds an armed rule can place a real order | Mandatory (estimated) badge plus SCR-058; detectors behind feature flags `metrics.iceberg_detector` / `.stop_run_detector` / `.absorption` until K01's calibration lands; explicit acknowledgement required before a detector may be the sole trigger of an armed live action (US-DET-006 NFR) |
| R9 Advice boundary | A "regime" badge reads like a recommendation | Regime is stated as a classification with numeric confidence and its sub-signals, never phrased as an action |
| R3 Real-time cost | Adding ~12 metric codes to `metrics.{symbol}` at 4 Hz for N symbols | One topic, server-side throttle (250 ms default), 1 Hz for regime; budget #3 re-measured in E25-Q03 |
| R2 Render performance | Panels rendering at tape rate | All rolling statistics computed backend-side; panels render <=4 Hz within a 1-1.5 ms budget (SCR-055/056 performance sections) |
| R6 Feed rot | Detector inputs depend on `orderbook.200` depth tiers; a tier change renormalises book speed | US-DET-003 requires the renormalisation to be annotated on the series |

## Technical notes / design
Engines live in `server/orderflow/` beside footprint, profile, cvd, imbalance, heatmap and tape. One `DetectorRegistry` holds `Detector` implementations with a uniform interface (`on_trade`, `on_book_delta`, `on_bar_close`, `emit(DetectorEvent)`), so replay (E26) and live share one code path with only the clock differing. Config defaults are exactly those published in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` schema `DetectorConfig` (iceberg `min_reloads=3`, `price_tolerance_ticks=0`, `window_ms=5000`; stop_run `lookback_bars=20`, `penetration_ticks=2`, `reversal_pct=60`; absorption `min_volume_multiple=3`, `max_price_move_ticks=1`).

## Security notes

title: UX research: how traders read speed, imbalance and estimated signals
body:
## Context
E25 introduces five new surfaces (SCR-055..059) whose value depends entirely on whether the owner and the account managers *believe and correctly interpret* them. Two interaction problems are genuinely new to the product and are not answered anywhere in the existing design system:

1. **How is an estimate communicated without being either ignored or over-trusted?** R2 exit criterion #4 makes the `(estimated)` badge mandatory, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` calls presenting a heuristic as certainty "a defect". But a badge that everyone learns to ignore fails the same requirement in practice. SCR-058's analytics deliberately track `methodology.opened` "so we can tell whether the honesty affordance is actually used" - this research sets the baseline expectation for that metric.
2. **What does a trader do with a regime label?** R9 (advice boundary) means the panel must read as classification-with-evidence. Whether real users read it that way is an empirical question.

Scheduled in Sprint 10, two sprints ahead of the consuming FE stories in Sprint 13, per the design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`: "Design runs ahead of engineering by >=2 sprints; no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan and 4-6 sessions with the owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`), each 45-60 minutes, using clickable prototypes or competitor tools as stimulus.
- Topics: reading speed-of-tape (gauge vs strip vs number; which window is the default mental model); scanning for imbalance stacks (list-first vs chart-first); interpreting a regime badge (does it read as advice?); comprehension of `(estimated)` (unprompted interpretation of the badge, then of the drawer).
- A comprehension test: show a stop-run marker with no explanation; ask what it means and how much the participant would trust it; then show SCR-058's content and re-ask.
- Findings report with prioritised design implications, verbatim quotes, and explicit recommendations for: the default window on SCR-055, list-vs-chart primacy on SCR-056, the wording of the regime badge, and the placement/affordance strength of the estimated badge.
- A recommended baseline target for the `methodology.opened` rate so the analytics have a yardstick.
- Handover briefing to the designers of D02-D04.

## Out of scope
Wireframes and visual design (D02-D04), usability testing of the built product (E25-D08 design QA / E25-Q04), quantitative A/B testing (no user base for it), any research on Android or a separate admin app (both out of scope for the plan).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed
  Given the research plan is approved
  Then at least four sessions are run with the owner and account-manager personas and are recorded with consent

Scenario: The estimated badge is tested for comprehension, not preference
  Then the report states, per participant, what they believed the badge meant before reading the drawer and after
  And it recommends a badge treatment supported by that evidence

Scenario: The advice boundary is tested
  Given participants are shown a regime badge
  Then the report states whether any participant read it as an instruction to trade
  And recommends wording that removes that reading

Scenario: Actionable implications
  Then every finding is paired with a concrete design implication assigned to D02, D03 or D04
  And the report names the default tape window, the SCR-056 primacy decision and the badge treatment

Scenario: Timely
  Then the report is published before the end of Sprint 10 so D02 can start on its findings
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the existing prototypes and, where nothing exists, competitor stimuli (the order-flow tools named in the research digests) rather than describing features verbally - verbal descriptions of an "estimated" signal produce agreement, not comprehension. Ask participants to think aloud while interpreting, and never ask "is this clear?" - ask them to explain it back.

Consent and recording per the research practice already used in the project; recordings stay in the internal research store.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Quality bar: findings are traceable to session evidence (timestamped quotes), and the report distinguishes observation from interpretation from recommendation.

## Security notes
Session recordings may capture participants' personal trading context and account details - classify as confidential, store in the internal research location only, redact account identifiers and balances from the published report, and never include real API credentials or screenshots containing them.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session run entirely with keyboard navigation and, if a participant with relevant assistive-technology experience is available, a screen-reader-led session; feed findings into D06.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
Recommends the baseline for the `methodology.opened{detector}` analytics event that SCR-058 emits.

## Definition of Done
Research plan approved; sessions run and recorded; findings report published and reviewed with the Chief Design Officer and the product owner; implications assigned to D02/D03/D04 as explicit checklist items; briefing delivered; report linked from this epic.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Informs D02, D03, D04 and D06.

body:
## Context
High-fidelity design for the three live panels. Each screens-catalogue entry ends with a **design sign-off acceptance checklist** that is the literal definition of done for this ticket:

**SCR-056**: event list + chart markers drawn and cross-highlighted; threshold and stacked-count controls with live effect; **side encoded by text as well as colour**; link from an event to the originating footprint cell; empty state ("no imbalances above 3:1 in this range"); stale-data shading.

**SCR-057**: current regime label with the mandatory *(estimated)* chip; **confidence expressed as a number plus words, never a bare colour**; sub-signal breakdown (trend strength, volatility, volume profile shape, tape speed, OI trend) each with its own value; regime-change history strip; "why this classification?" link to SCR-058; insufficient-history state.

Sprint 11, two sprints ahead of the Sprint-13 build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for SCR-055, SCR-056 and SCR-057 in every documented state, on the design-system tokens (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`) in both themes and at all supported densities.
- CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge, CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane, CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator, CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip specified to component-catalogue level (props, states, tokens) and contributed back through D05.
- Non-colour encodings for every signal-bearing element: threshold bands (pattern/weight), imbalance side (text + glyph), regime confidence (number + word).
- Motion specification: what animates, how long, and what does not animate at all - given the 4 Hz update cadence, most of these panels must not animate on value change.
- Empty, warming-up, stale, disconnected and insufficient-data states drawn with final copy.
- Redlines and token references for handoff (D07).

## Out of scope
SCR-058 and SCR-059 (D04), design-system primitives themselves (D05), a11y review (D06), implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Catalogue checklists satisfied
  Then every item on the SCR-055, SCR-056 and SCR-057 design sign-off acceptance checklists is demonstrably satisfied by a frame

Scenario: No colour-only meaning
  Given every element that carries meaning on these three panels
  Then each has a non-colour carrier, verified by rendering the frames in greyscale

Scenario: Estimated chip is mandatory on regime
  Then SCR-057 shows the (estimated) chip in every regime state, including insufficient data

Scenario: Confidence is a number
  Then confidence is drawn as a numeric value accompanied by a word, never as a colour or dots alone

Scenario: Motion respects the update cadence
  Then the motion spec states which elements do not animate, and no element animates on every 4 Hz update

Scenario: Both themes, all densities
  Then every frame exists in light and dark themes at each supported density with contrast checked
```

## Technical notes / design
Design against the published cadences: SCR-055 updates at 4 Hz, SCR-057 at most 1 Hz and renders only on change. A design that implies smooth interpolation between 4 Hz samples is asking engineering to violate the panel's 1 ms budget.

The estimated chip on SCR-055 belongs to the **book-speed classification only** (US-DET-003), not to trades/sec and notional/sec, which are exact - misapplying the chip devalues it.

No real account data in frames. SCR-057 copy must contain no advisory or imperative phrasing (R9) - this is a design-time control, checked at sign-off.

Contrast ratios verified for every token pairing used; focus states drawn for every interactive element; the text readout is drawn as a first-class element on SCR-055 (it is the primary accessible value, not a tooltip); SCR-056's table is drawn as the primary representation. Full review in D06.

title: Hi-fi design: methodology drawer and detector settings (SCR-058, SCR-059)
body:
## Context
High-fidelity design for the two surfaces that carry the epic's honesty and safety obligations.

**SCR-058** sign-off checklist: one section per estimated signal (iceberg, stop-run, absorption, queue position, order-count footprint, regime, liquidity cluster); each section states what it infers, from what data, the exact heuristic and thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain; the words "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact" appear in each section; link to the detector settings.

**SCR-059** sign-off checklist: every detector with its thresholds, look-back and minimum-confidence controls; **a warning listing armed rules that depend on the detector being changed**; reset-to-default per detector; *(estimated)* framing repeated; validation messages for out-of-range values.

SCR-059's audit note explains why its design is a safety matter: detector changes are audited "because detector output can feed armed rules that place orders".

Sprint 11, two sprints ahead of the Sprint-13 build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for SCR-058 (drawer, one section per estimated signal, plus the degraded state where current thresholds cannot be fetched) and SCR-059 (dialog, per-detector fieldsets, presets, explicit thresholds, symbol scope, backtest preview, all validation and state variants).
- Final copy for all UI chrome, validation messages ("Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %"-style, matching the published bounds), the high-sensitivity warning, and the armed-rule warning - drafted with the content owner and aligned with E25-T07's methodology wording.
- The armed-rule warning designed as a blocking confirmation listing the affected rules, plus the fail-safe variant for when dependent rules cannot be enumerated.
- The apply state machine drawn: idle -> applying -> applied, and applying -> failed-with-restore; "applied" never appears before backend confirmation.
- Disabled-missing-dependency state with the exact missing dependency named and the one-click start-recording action.
- Per-symbol override indication.
- Reading-comprehension pass on SCR-058: plain-language summary first, technical detail second, glossary links for jargon.
- Redlines and token references for handoff (D07).

## Out of scope
SCR-055..057 (D03), authoring the methodology *content* itself (E25-T07 owns the substance; this ticket owns its presentation and the chrome copy), design-system primitives (D05), a11y review (D06), the rule-engine UI (E36/E37).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One section per estimated signal
  Then SCR-058 has a section for each of iceberg, stop-run, absorption, queue position, order-count footprint, regime and liquidity cluster
  And each contains the sentence that this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact

Scenario: Thresholds in force
  Then SCR-058 shows the thresholds currently in force, visually distinct from documented defaults

Scenario: Armed-rule warning
  Given a detector whose output is used by an armed rule
  Then SCR-059 is drawn with a blocking confirmation listing those rules before a change can be applied
  And a fail-safe variant is drawn for when the rule list cannot be fetched

Scenario: Never optimistic
  Then the apply state machine is drawn with applying and applied as distinct states, and applied is only reachable after backend confirmation
  And a failed apply is drawn restoring the previous values with the error shown

Scenario: Validation
  Then each numeric control is drawn with its unit, default and permitted range, and an out-of-range message naming the range

Scenario: Missing dependency
  Then a detector disabled for a missing dependency is drawn naming the exact dependency with a one-click start-recording action
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the real published bounds from `DetectorConfig` in every frame (iceberg min_reloads 2-50, window_ms 200-60000, stop_run lookback_bars 2-500, penetration_ticks 1-100, reversal_pct 0-100, absorption min_volume_multiple 1-50, max_price_move_ticks 0-50). Designing with invented ranges produces validation copy that has to be rewritten during the build.

SCR-058 is a reading surface, so typography and line length matter more than density here - deliberately break from the trading-dense defaults and specify the exception in the tokens.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Verification: copy reviewed by the content owner; every published bound represented; a designer walks the apply state machine against the SCR-059 performance contract.

## Security notes
The armed-rule warning and the non-optimistic apply are security controls in visual form; omitting or softening either in design would remove a control the threat model (E25-X01) relies on. Frames must show that a rejected change restores previous values rather than leaving an ambiguous state.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-058: plain-language first, proper heading hierarchy for screen-reader navigation, no jargon without a glossary link. SCR-059: per-detector fieldsets with legends, units and defaults visible, validation messages associated with their field, focus trap and restore drawn. Full review in D06.

## Performance notes
SCR-058 opens in <=150 ms with no streaming subscriptions - the design must not require live data to render. SCR-059's backtest preview is drawn with a progressive loading state so it never blocks the dialog.

## Observability
`methodology.opened{detector}` annotated on SCR-058; `detector.enabled_changed` / `detector.threshold_changed` annotated on SCR-059 with a note that these are audited server-side.

## Definition of Done
Both screens' catalogue sign-off checklists satisfied; copy reviewed by the content owner and aligned with T07; both themes and all densities; contrast checked; reviewed and signed off by the design lead, the product owner and a security reviewer (for the armed-rule warning); sign-off recorded (gate for E25-S04 and E25-S05).

Five components in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` are introduced or materially extended by this epic, and one of them - **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** - is load-bearing for a release exit criterion. CMP-069 InfoPanel's catalogue entry defines it as "the linked methodology drawer referenced by **every** '(estimated)' chip (CMP-011 estimated variant) - explains heuristic detector logic in plain language", and CMP-134 DetectorEventCard's a11y note makes the estimated chip **mandatory** on the card.

If these components are specified once, correctly, every surface in E25 (and E18, E21, E22's clustering, E24) inherits the honesty behaviour for free. If they are not, each surface reimplements it and one of them will get it wrong - which R2 classifies as a P1 bug.

Sprint 10, ahead of D03/D04 which compose them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**: canonical spec - variants (inline chip, marker affordance, section header), sizes, tokens, the required `onOpenMethodology(detector)` binding, and the rule that it is never purely decorative and never colour-only.
- **CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge** and **CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane**: props (`windowSec`, side split, threshold classification string, z-score, warming-up state), states and tokens; the text readout specified as a first-class element, not a tooltip.
- **CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator**: price range, direction, depth, ratio, status (active/tested/broken) with text carriers for each.
- **CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip**: regime label, numeric confidence, mandatory estimated variant (its catalogue entry already says it "inherits CMP-011 estimated variant").
- **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard**: card composition (CMP-050) with the mandatory estimated chip, the parameter-snapshot block, and hover/focus parity.
- Confirmation that **CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots** is specified as a supplement to a numeric value, never a replacement.
- Storybook specifications (states to be implemented) and token additions, contributed to the design-system library and the component catalogue.
- Greyscale and contrast verification for every new component.

## Out of scope
Screen-level design (D03/D04), implementation of the components (done inside the consuming stories), changes to CMP-049 Table / CMP-043 Dialog / CMP-046 Drawer base contracts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One canonical estimated badge
  Then CMP-227 is specified once with all its variants
  And the spec requires an accessible label and the methodology binding on every variant
  And no variant conveys its meaning through colour alone

Scenario: Confidence is never a bare visual
  Then CMP-133 and CMP-032 are specified such that a numeric confidence value is always present alongside any dots or colour

Scenario: Detector card mandates the chip
  Then CMP-134's spec makes the estimated chip mandatory and includes the parameter-snapshot block

Scenario: Text carriers
  Given CMP-132's direction and status
  Then each is specified with a text carrier in addition to any colour or glyph

Scenario: Catalogue updated
  Then docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md entries for CMP-131, CMP-132, CMP-133, CMP-134, CMP-187 and CMP-227 match the delivered specs

Scenario: Contrast
  Then every token pairing used by these components meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, verified and recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Specify CMP-227's API as `({ detector, variant, size })` with the drawer binding supplied by context, so a consumer cannot render the badge without it being actionable. That constraint is what makes E25-S04's "opens from any estimated badge" acceptance criterion structurally true rather than dependent on each screen remembering to wire it.

Keep the estimated treatment consistent but not shouty: it appears on many surfaces at once (footprint order-count, heatmap queue position, iceberg, stop-run, absorption, regime, trade clustering), so a heavy treatment would dominate the interface and train users to filter it out - a point D01 tests empirically.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Verification: greyscale render of each component; contrast report; a designer and a frontend engineer jointly confirm each spec is implementable with existing tokens.

## Security notes
None directly; the estimated badge is itself a risk-communication control for R7 and R9, so weakening its spec has downstream safety consequences.

## Accessibility notes
Each component spec must state its accessible name, role, keyboard behaviour and focus appearance. CMP-227 must be a real button (it opens a drawer), not a decorative span. CMP-134 must be reachable by keyboard, not hover-only.

## Performance notes
These components render on streaming panels at up to 4 Hz; specs must avoid shadows, blurs and transitions that would breach the 1-1.5 ms panel budgets.

## Observability
CMP-227 emits `methodology.opened{detector}` through its binding, so instrumentation is inherited rather than reimplemented per surface.

## Definition of Done
Specs delivered for all six components; component catalogue entries updated; tokens contributed; contrast and greyscale verification recorded; reviewed and approved by the design-system team lead and a frontend code owner; Storybook story list agreed with engineering.

title: Accessibility design review of SCR-055..059 before handoff
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA as the product standard, and the R2 quality gates require "a11y pass on every new view". Reviewing accessibility *before* handoff is cheaper than auditing it after the build (E25-Q04 still audits the built product, but it should find little).

These five screens have specific hazards: two of them are value-streaming panels where colour is the natural encoding for direction and intensity; one is a classification badge where colour is the natural encoding for regime; and two are dense forms. The screens catalogue already prescribes the mitigations - text-first readouts, real tables, numeric confidence, text side encoding - and this review verifies the hi-fi designs actually deliver them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Structured review of every D03 and D04 frame against WCAG 2.2 AA and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Colour-independence check: greyscale rendering of every frame; every meaning-bearing element must survive it.
- Contrast measurement for every token pairing in both themes, including the non-text 3:1 requirement for graphical objects (gauges, threshold bands, markers).
- Focus-order specification per screen, including the SCR-056 table row cursor, the SCR-059 dialog focus trap and restore, and the SCR-058 drawer's focus-to-section behaviour.
- Screen-reader narrative: what is announced, in what order, and what is suppressed - explicitly including SCR-055's "42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean" readout, the 5-second announcement throttle, and SCR-056's "bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1" ratio sentence.
- Target sizes and spacing checked against WCAG 2.2's target-size criterion for the dense settings dialog.
- Reduced-motion variants for anything the D03 motion spec animates.
- A findings list with each item either fixed in the frames before sign-off or raised as an accepted, documented exception.

## Out of scope
Automated axe-core testing of the built UI (E25-Q04), remediation of components outside this epic, the chart engine's DOM-mirror mechanism itself (E11; this review only confirms detector markers use it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Greyscale survival
  Given every hi-fi frame rendered in greyscale
  Then every element that carries meaning remains distinguishable

Scenario: Contrast
  Then every text pairing meets 4.5 to 1 (or 3 to 1 for large text) and every graphical object meets 3 to 1, in both themes, with measurements recorded

Scenario: Announcements specified
  Then each screen has a written screen-reader narrative, including what is deliberately not announced
  And SCR-055's throttle of at most one threshold announcement per five seconds is specified

Scenario: Focus
  Then focus order, visible focus appearance, dialog trap and restore, and drawer focus-to-section are specified for all five screens

Scenario: Findings resolved
  Then every finding is fixed in the frames or recorded as an approved exception with a rationale
  And no finding of severity high remains open at sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Review against the real announcement sentences rather than generic labels - the screens catalogue already wrote them, and a review that accepts "the gauge is announced" loses the specificity that makes the panel usable without sight.

Pay particular attention to SCR-056: its catalogue entry insists the canvas heat strip "is never the only representation". Confirm the table is drawn as primary and the canvas as supplementary, not the reverse.

This ticket *is* the accessibility work. Standard: `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, WCAG 2.2 AA.

Reduced-motion variants must not introduce additional render work; the preferred implementation is to remove animation, not replace it.

N/A.

Review completed on all five screens; contrast and greyscale evidence attached; focus orders and screen-reader narratives written into the frames; all findings resolved or formally accepted; signed off by the accessibility lead; result is a precondition for D07 handoff.

title: Design QA sweep of the built detector surfaces against the specs
body:
## Context
R2's design quality gate requires a "design-QA sweep" on the new views. This ticket compares the built SCR-055..059 and the chart detector markers against the D03/D04/D06/D07 specifications, in both themes, at all densities, and files the discrepancies.

Because the epic's honesty requirement is enforced visually, this sweep also performs the **badge audit**: every surface that renders a heuristic value must show the `(estimated)` badge, and every badge must open SCR-058 at the correct section. R2 exit criterion #4 makes a miss here a P1 bug.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen-by-screen visual comparison against the signed-off frames: spacing, type, tokens, states, empty/stale/disconnected/warming-up/insufficient-data treatments, focus appearance.
- Both themes; every supported density; the window sizes the workspace supports.

- Motion and reduced-motion verification.
- Copy verification against the D07 copy deck, including validation messages and the armed-rule warning wording.
- Findings filed as bugs with severity, screenshots and the frame reference; blocking items fixed before the epic closes.
- Design sign-off statement on the built product.

## Out of scope
Functional testing (E25-Q01/Q02), accessibility audit (E25-Q04), performance (E25-Q03), redesign - findings are discrepancies against the spec, not new design opinions.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state verified
  Then each documented state of each of the five screens has been observed in the built product and compared with its frame

Scenario: Badge audit passes
  Given every surface that renders a heuristic value
  Then it shows the (estimated) badge, and activating it opens SCR-058 at that detector's section
  And any miss is filed as a P1

Scenario: Both themes and all densities
```

## Observability

title: Spike: calibrate iceberg/stop-run/absorption heuristics on recorded data
body:
## Context
The three L2-derived detectors in this epic (absorption, iceberg, stop-run) ship with numeric defaults already published in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` schema `DetectorConfig`: iceberg `min_reloads=3`, `price_tolerance_ticks=0`, `window_ms=5000`; stop_run `lookback_bars=20`, `penetration_ticks=2`, `reversal_pct=60`; absorption `min_volume_multiple=3`, `max_price_move_ticks=1`. Those numbers came from research digests, not from CandleViewer's own recorded Bybit data. Bybit's public feed is anonymous and aggregated and exposes no L3/MBO data, so iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences, not observations. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` makes `confidence="estimated"` mandatory for every heuristic and states plainly that "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface that shows one of these values must render CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the detector methodology drawer.

R2 exit criterion #4 and the roadmap risk table make detector *credibility* a release gate, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` keeps `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector` and `metrics.absorption` behind feature flags defaulting to `false` precisely because "heuristics behind flags until thresholds are tuned". This spike produces the tuning evidence that lets those flags be turned on and that fills the false-positive-mode sections of SCR-058.

Timebox: **3 days, 2 engineers max.** Output is a written decision, not production code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A notebook/script under `research/detector-calibration/` (DuckDB over the Parquet cold tier, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`) that replays at least three recorded BTCUSDT and one ETHUSDT symbol-day through prototype implementations of the three heuristics.
- Fixture set selection: normal session, high-volatility burst, thin-book period (the integration fixture classes named in roadmap section 6.4).
- For each detector and each candidate parameter set: event count per hour, inter-event spacing distribution, and a manually labelled sample of 50 events per detector classified as plausible / implausible / undecidable by an order-flow-literate reviewer, reading the tape and book around each event.
- Recommended default parameter values and the low/medium/high sensitivity presets required by SCR-059.
- A written list of **false-positive modes per detector** in the exact wording to be used by `DetectorMethodology.false_positive_modes` (`/detectors/methodology`).
- Measured per-event CPU cost to size budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU per symbol).
- A short decision record appended to the epic (and an ADR only if the spike concludes a published default must change).

## Out of scope
Production implementation (E25-T03/T04), UI, alerting, any change to the OpenAPI defaults without an accompanying ADR, machine-learned classifiers (explicitly not in R2 scope).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Recommendation exists
  Given three recorded BTCUSDT symbol-days and one ETHUSDT symbol-day
  When the calibration script runs each detector over each day at three candidate parameter sets
  Then the spike report recommends one default and three sensitivity presets per detector with the measured event rate for each

Scenario: False-positive modes are named
  Then each detector has at least two concretely described false-positive modes, each supported by a timestamp in the fixture data where it occurs

Scenario: Defaults are either confirmed or challenged in writing
  Given the published DetectorConfig defaults
  Then the report states for each parameter whether the recorded data supports it, and where it does not, proposes a value and raises an ADR

Scenario: Cost is known
  Then the report states measured CPU microseconds per trade and per book delta for each detector, and whether the combined cost fits budget #11

Scenario: Timebox respected
  Given the three-day timebox expires
  Then the report is published with whatever evidence exists and explicitly lists what remains unknown, rather than being extended silently
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype in Python against the Parquet tier so the run is reproducible and does not need a live feed. Iceberg prototype: track per-price resting size from `orderbook.200` deltas; count a "reload" when size at a price falls below a fraction of its prior value and returns to within `price_tolerance_ticks` and a size tolerance within `window_ms`; score = reload count. Absorption prototype: aggressive volume at a price over a window exceeding `min_volume_multiple` times the rolling median while price advance stays within `max_price_move_ticks`. Stop-run prototype: swing extreme over `lookback_bars`, penetration by `penetration_ticks`, then retracement of `reversal_pct` of the penetration excursion within the reversion window.

Label the sample blind where possible (reviewer sees the market context, not the detector's own score) to avoid confirming the heuristic with itself.

## Test plan
N/A for shipping tests; the calibration script itself must be deterministic (fixed fixture list, no wall-clock) and re-runnable by another engineer from the README in `research/detector-calibration/`. Reproduce-twice check: two runs produce identical event counts.

## Security notes
Fixture data is public market data. Do not copy recorded data outside the repo's data volume; the notebook must read from the configured data path, never from a pasted export. No credentials in the notebook.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - internal research artefact. Charts in the report must have a table alternative so the findings are reviewable by everyone.

## Performance notes
Measure per-event cost (microseconds per trade / per book delta) against budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU sustained per actively recorded symbol) and budget #8 (<=300 MB resident per symbol) - the iceberg detector's per-price state is the memory risk.

## Observability
None shipped. The report must state which counters E25-T03/T04 should emit (at minimum `orderflow_detector_events_total{detector,symbol}` and a per-detector suppressed-by-cooldown counter).

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 5.2: question answered in writing; report committed under `research/detector-calibration/`; recommendation reviewed by the M9 owner and the architect; follow-up tickets (parameter changes, ADR) raised; timebox respected; the spike's conclusions are linked from E25-T03 and E25-T04.

title: Author the black-box test plan and exploratory charters for detectors
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review. This epic needs one that is unusually explicit about *honesty* and *determinism*, because those are R2 exit criteria (#4 and #7) rather than ordinary quality attributes, and neither is naturally covered by functional testing of the happy path.

The roadmap also names the integration fixture classes for R2: "normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol". Detector behaviour differs sharply across them - a thin-book symbol is the false-positive-rich case for iceberg, a volatility burst is the sweep-rich case for stop-run - so the plan must exercise each deliberately.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan covering all nine DET stories, organised by story group: (a) tape and book speed, (b) imbalance stacks, (c) absorption/iceberg/stop-run, (d) regime, (e) configuration and methodology.
- Per group: preconditions, test data/fixture, steps, expected results, and the failure and edge cases named in each story's Gherkin (idle market, warming up, depth-tier change, no-reversion, insufficient data, missing dependency, out-of-range value, unauthorised change).
- The **honesty checklist** required by the R2 quality gates: "per estimated view: badge present, popover accurate, thresholds visible in the inspector" - enumerated per surface, executable by a tester with no knowledge of the implementation.
- Exploratory charters (session-based, 90 minutes each): "explore detector behaviour on a thin-book symbol looking for implausible events"; "explore the settings dialog looking for ways to apply a change without the armed-rule warning"; "explore the estimated affordance looking for any heuristic value with no badge"; "explore state transitions during WS disconnect and resync looking for values that keep updating when they should be stale".
- Fixture requirements handed to the engineering tickets: which recorded windows are needed and what each must contain (a stop-run, a multi-reload level, an absorption event, at least two regime transitions).
- Traceability table mapping every test case to a US-DET id and every US-DET id to at least one case.
- Entry and exit criteria for QA on this epic, and the definition of the regression pack that E25-Q05 will run.

## Out of scope
Executing the plan (done through the sprint and finalised in E25-Q05), automated E2E implementation (E25-Q02), performance scripts (E25-Q03), the a11y audit (E25-Q04), unit tests (owned by the engineering tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full story coverage
  Then every one of US-DET-001 to US-DET-009 maps to at least one test case
  And every Gherkin scenario in those stories maps to a test case, including the failure and edge cases

Scenario: Honesty checklist is executable
  Then the plan lists every surface that renders a heuristic value with a per-surface check for badge presence, popover accuracy and threshold visibility
  And a tester with no implementation knowledge can execute it

Scenario: Fixture classes covered
  Then the plan exercises normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect and resync, sequence gap and thin-book symbol

Scenario: Exploratory charters defined
  Then at least four time-boxed charters are defined with a mission and a debrief template

Scenario: Reviewed
  Then the plan is reviewed and accepted by the product owner and the M9 engineer
```

## Technical notes / design
Write the honesty checklist as a table of `(surface, element, expected badge, expected drawer section)` so it is mechanical to run and can later be partly automated in E25-Q02. Its value is that it does not depend on a tester remembering the rule.

For determinism, the plan's role is to specify the *observable* check (two replays of the same window produce the same event list in the UI); the automated equality assertion lives in E25-Q03.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse cases from E25-X01 as test cases: unauthorised threshold change, threshold change without the armed-rule warning, and detector-driven armed action without acknowledgement. QA verifies controls, not merely features.

The plan references E25-Q04 for the audit but includes basic keyboard-operability checks in every functional case, so a keyboard regression is caught during normal testing rather than only at audit time.

The plan defines the observational perf checks (panel feels responsive at 4 Hz; no visible jank when markers cluster) and defers measurement to E25-Q03.

title: Add Playwright E2E coverage for the detector surfaces and flows
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E (Playwright, web and Electron) above the integration layer in the pyramid, reserved for the flows whose breakage would be most costly. For E25 those are: the estimated-badge-to-methodology flow (an R2 exit criterion), the detector-settings apply flow (a security-relevant path), and the imbalance-row-to-chart navigation (the panel's entire purpose).

Tests run against a **recorded fixture replayed through the normal pipeline**, not against live Bybit, so they are deterministic and can produce stale, disconnected and warming-up states on demand.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under the existing E2E suite, tagged `@e25`, running in both the web and Electron targets per the testing strategy.
- Flow 1 - **estimated affordance**: from SCR-055's book-speed badge, SCR-057's regime badge and a chart detector marker, activating the badge opens SCR-058 scrolled and focused at the correct section; the section shows the thresholds currently in force; the link to SCR-059 works.
- Flow 2 - **settings apply**: open SCR-059, enter an out-of-range value and see the range-naming validation; enter a valid value; see the armed-rule warning when a dependent armed rule exists; apply; observe the applying-then-applied sequence (never applied first); verify the change is reflected in SCR-058's thresholds-in-force and in an audit entry.
- Flow 3 - **imbalance navigation**: a stack appears in SCR-056 within the fixture; selecting the row by mouse and by keyboard jumps and highlights the chart zone; the empty state appears when thresholds are raised beyond the fixture's stacks.
- Flow 4 - **degraded states**: WS disconnect mid-fixture leaves panels showing stale/disconnected rather than stale values presented as live; resync restores updates without duplicating rows.
- Flow 5 - **regime transition**: a transition in the fixture updates the badge and the history strip, and `/market/regime/explain` content matches the badge.
- Flow 6 - **honesty sweep (automated part of the Q01 checklist)**: a test that walks every surface listed in the checklist table and asserts a badge with the expected detector id is present.
- Fixture management: reuse the recorded windows produced for E25-T03/T04 golden fixtures rather than creating a parallel set.
- CI wiring, deflake budget, and documentation of how to run the suite locally.

## Out of scope
Unit and component tests (owned by the stories), performance and determinism measurement (E25-Q03), the a11y audit (E25-Q04), backend contract tests (owned by T01/T02/T05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite runs deterministically
  Given the recorded fixture is replayed through the normal pipeline
  Then the E2E suite passes on ten consecutive CI runs with no flakes
  And it does not contact the live exchange

Scenario: Estimated flow
  Then activating an estimated badge on the tape panel, the regime panel and a chart marker each opens the methodology drawer at the correct section with focus moved to that section

Scenario: Settings apply
  Then an out-of-range value is rejected with a message naming the range
  And a valid change shows the armed-rule warning where a dependent armed rule exists
  And the applied state appears only after backend confirmation
  And the change is visible in the methodology drawer's thresholds in force

Scenario: Imbalance navigation by keyboard
  Then a stack row can be reached and activated using only the keyboard, and the chart zone is highlighted

Scenario: Degraded state honesty
  Given the WebSocket disconnects
  Then the panels show a disconnected or stale state rather than continuing to present the last value as current

Scenario: Honesty sweep automated
  Then the suite asserts, for every surface in the test plan's checklist table, that the expected estimated badge is present
```

## Technical notes / design
Drive states through the replay pipeline and a controllable WS proxy rather than through UI stubbing, so the test exercises the real subscription and decode path - the failure modes this epic cares about (stale presented as live, duplicate rows after resync) only appear there.

Select elements by role and accessible name wherever possible; it keeps the E2E suite honest about accessibility as a side effect and makes it resilient to styling changes.

Keep each flow under 90 seconds; parallelise by flow. Quarantine policy per the testing strategy: a flaky test is fixed or removed, never retried indefinitely.

## Test plan
This ticket is test work. Self-verification: ten consecutive green runs; a deliberate mutation (remove a badge; make apply optimistic) must fail the suite - record that mutation check in the PR.

## Security notes
Flow 2 asserts a control, not merely a feature; add a negative case where a Viewer-role session cannot apply a change and the UI does not offer it. Test credentials come from the CI secret store, never from the repo; fixtures contain no account data.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard paths are first-class test cases (SCR-056 row navigation, SCR-059 dialog focus trap and restore, SCR-058 focus-to-section). Role/name-based selectors mean a broken accessible name breaks the suite.

## Performance notes
Suite runtime budget: <=8 minutes in CI for the `@e25` tag. Measurement of product performance belongs to E25-Q03.

## Observability
Assert the analytics events fire for the flows covered (`methodology.opened`, `detector.threshold_changed`, `imbalance.event_clicked`, `regime.explain_opened`).

## Definition of Done
Specs merged and green in CI on both web and Electron targets; ten consecutive runs without flakes; mutation check recorded; fixtures shared with the golden-fixture set rather than duplicated; local run instructions documented; traceability updated in the Q01 plan.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-Q01 (the plan defines what is worth automating), E25-S01 and E25-S05 (the surfaces must exist). Feeds E25-Q05.

## Branch
`test/detectors-e2e`. PR size guidance: one PR per flow group.

## References

title: Determinism, perf and chaos testing for the detector pipeline
body:
## Context
Three R2 gates land on this ticket.

- **Determinism** (exit criterion #7, quality gate "Determinism"): "Detector outputs are reproducible: replaying the same recorded window twice yields identical detector events."
- **Performance** (exit criterion #2 and #9): the full order-flow scene must hold p95 <=16.6 ms and never drop below 30 fps (budgets #1, #2) *with the detector marker layer added*, and WS tick to screen p95 must stay <100 ms (budget #3, hard R2 gate) with the detector metric set on the subscription.
- **Chaos** (quality gate "Integration" fixtures): WS disconnect and resync, sequence gap, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018 - detectors must not emit phantom events across a gap and must not present stale values as live.

This ticket also validates the E25-K01 calibration in the built system, which is the precondition for turning the `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector` and `metrics.absorption` feature flags on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Determinism harness** in CI: replay a recorded symbol-day twice through the full pipeline; assert the emitted detector event streams (absorption, iceberg, stop_run, regime transitions, imbalance stacks) are identical, field by field including `params_snapshot`; assert the same across two different machines/CI runners.
- **Golden-fixture drift test** wired into CI: committed expected event streams; any drift fails the build (quality gate "Correctness").
- **Frontend perf benchmark**: the full R2 scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD pane) plus the detector marker layer at worst-case event density, asserting budgets #1 and #2; plus per-panel render budgets (SCR-055 <=1 ms at 4 Hz, SCR-056 <=1.5 ms at 4 Hz with a full 2 000-entry buffer, SCR-057 <=1 ms and zero renders on unchanged verdicts).
- **Budget #3 measurement** with the detector metric set added to `metrics.{symbol}`: backend receipt timestamp to paint timestamp, p95 <100 ms and p99 <250 ms.
- **Backend load/soak**: k6/Locust driving N symbols with the full detector set enabled for a sustained window; assert budgets #6 (<=20 ms fan-out add-on), #8 (<=300 MB per symbol), #11 (<=0.5 vCPU per symbol) and flat memory over the run.
- **Chaos scenarios**: WS disconnect and resync, sequence gap forcing a book resnapshot, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018; assert no phantom detector events are emitted across the gap, panels show stale/disconnected honestly, and detector state recovers without duplicate events after resync.
- **Calibration validation**: event rates per detector on the fixture set compared against the bands recommended by E25-K01; a written go/no-go for each feature flag.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E25-Q02), a11y (E25-Q04), the chart engine's own baseline benchmarks (E11), replay-engine determinism itself (E26 - this ticket asserts detector determinism *given* the replay clock).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Determinism across runs and machines
  Given the same recorded symbol-day
  When it is replayed twice on the same runner and once on a different runner
  Then all three detector event streams are identical field by field, including the parameter snapshots

Scenario: Golden fixtures guard against drift
  Given committed expected event streams
  When a change alters detector output
  Then CI fails with a diff naming the detector and the first differing event

Scenario: Frame budget with detectors
  Given the full R2 order-flow scene plus the detector marker layer at worst-case density
  Then p95 frame time is at most 16.6 milliseconds and the frame rate never drops below 30 frames per second

Scenario: WS tick to screen
  Given the detector metric set is subscribed
  Then WS tick to screen is under 100 milliseconds at p95 and under 250 milliseconds at p99

Scenario: No phantom events across a gap
  Given a sequence gap forces a book resnapshot
  Then no detector event is emitted for the gap period
  And after resync detection resumes without duplicating events

Scenario: Soak is flat
  Given the detector set runs for the soak duration across N symbols
  Then memory is flat, CPU stays within budget and no messages are lost

Scenario: Flags have a written verdict
  Then each of the three detector feature flags has a documented go or no-go based on measured event rates against the calibration bands
```

## Technical notes / design
Determinism comparison must be on the *serialised event stream*, not on aggregate counts - counts can match while ordering or magnitudes differ. Sort keys are defined by the engines (`(ts_ms, price, detector)`), so an ordering difference is a genuine defect, not a test artefact.

For the perf benchmark, reuse the existing engine benchmark harness in CI rather than building a second one; add the detector marker layer as a scene variant so the comparison against the no-detector baseline is direct and a regression is attributable.

Chaos scenarios are driven through the WS proxy used by E25-Q02 so both suites share one mechanism.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test work. Its own quality bar: each assertion must fail when the corresponding behaviour is deliberately broken - record those negative checks (introduce a wall-clock call to break determinism; disable the density clamp to break the frame budget) in the PR.

## Security notes
The load test doubles as a DoS probe for the concerns raised in E25-X01: unbounded `metrics[]` selection, oversized REST backfill ranges, and repeated recompute requests. Assert the caps (12 metrics, bounded range, rate limit) hold under load and return errors rather than degrading the service.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (E25-Q04 owns accessibility), except that the perf benchmark must run with the DOM-mirror enabled, since it is part of the shipped cost.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: #1, #2, #3, #6, #8, #11, plus the per-panel render budgets from the screens catalogue. All are hard gates for R2 except #11 (tracked).

## Observability
The harness exports its measurements to the CI performance dashboard so regressions are visible over time rather than only as a pass/fail. Detector event-rate metrics are captured per fixture for the calibration comparison.

## Definition of Done
Determinism, golden-fixture, perf, load/soak and chaos suites merged and running in CI; all asserted budgets green; negative checks recorded; the feature-flag go/no-go written and reviewed with the M9 owner and the product owner; results linked from the epic and fed into the R2 PRR.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-Q01 (plan), E25-T03, E25-T04, E25-T05 (detectors to measure) and E25-S06 (the marker layer that affects the frame budget). Feeds E25-Q05 and the R2 PRR.

title: Accessibility audit of SCR-055..059 and the detector markers
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes; R2's quality gates require an a11y pass on every new view, with the specific demand that "heatmap has a non-colour alternative" and that canvas-based views are reachable through the DOM mirror. E25's screens have their own explicit obligations in the screens catalogue, and this audit verifies the built product against them rather than against a generic checklist.

E25-D06 reviewed the designs; this ticket audits the implementation. If D06 did its job, this audit should find little - and if it finds a lot, that is a signal about the handoff, which should be recorded.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated scans wired into CI for SCR-055, SCR-056, SCR-057, SCR-058, SCR-059 and the detector event card, in both themes; zero violations of serious or critical severity.
- Manual screen-reader passes (the project's primary screen reader plus one alternative) covering: SCR-055's text readout as the primary accessible value and the once-per-5-seconds throttle on threshold announcements; SCR-056's table-first structure and the "bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1" ratio sentence; SCR-057's text-first badge and numeric confidence; SCR-058's heading structure, focus-to-section and focus restore; SCR-059's fieldsets, units, defaults, validation association and the announcement of new effective thresholds.
- Keyboard-only pass: every control reachable and operable; SCR-056 row cursor and activation; SCR-059 focus trap and restore; chart detector markers reachable through the DOM mirror with the card content announced.
- Colour-independence verification on the built UI (greyscale and a colour-vision-deficiency simulation): threshold bands, imbalance side, regime, marker types.
- Contrast verification on rendered pixels, including graphical objects at 3:1.
- Target-size and spacing check on SCR-059.
- Reduced-motion verification.
- Findings filed with severity and WCAG success-criterion references; blocking findings fixed and re-verified before the epic closes; an audit report with a statement of conformance for these screens.

## Out of scope
Accessibility of screens outside this epic; the DOM-mirror mechanism itself (E11, though failures found here are raised against it); design-time review (E25-D06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated scans clean
  Then axe-core reports zero serious or critical violations on all five screens in both themes, and the scans run in CI

Scenario: Screen-reader narrative matches the specification
  Then each screen is announced as specified in the handoff, including the tape panel's sentence readout and the imbalance ratio sentence
  And no more than one threshold announcement occurs in any five-second period

Scenario: Keyboard-only operation
  Then every function of all five screens and the chart detector markers is operable by keyboard alone with a visible focus indicator

Scenario: No colour-only meaning
  Given greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulations of the built screens
  Then every meaning-bearing element remains distinguishable

Scenario: Markers reachable
  Then detector markers on the chart are reachable through the DOM mirror and their event card content is announced

Scenario: Findings resolved
  Then every blocking finding is fixed and re-verified, and the audit report records a conformance statement for these screens
```

## Technical notes / design
Test with real data flowing (replay fixture), not static stories - announcement throttling, live-region behaviour and focus stability under streaming updates are exactly what breaks, and a static Storybook pass will not reveal it.

Where a finding stems from a shared component (CMP-227, CMP-049, CMP-043), raise it against the design-system component so every consumer benefits, and note the cross-epic impact.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Evidence: axe-core CI reports, screen-reader session recordings or transcripts, greyscale/CVD screenshots, contrast measurements, and the findings register.

## Security notes
Confirm the SCR-059 armed-rule confirmation is fully operable by keyboard and screen reader - a safety control that cannot be operated non-visually is not a control for every user.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the accessibility work; standard is `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Performance notes
Confirm the DOM mirror and live regions do not breach the panel render budgets; if they do, hand the measurement to E25-Q03 rather than silently trading accessibility away.

## Observability
Audit results recorded in the accessibility tracking sheet so R5 hardening can see the trend across epics.

## Definition of Done
axe-core scans in CI and clean; manual screen-reader and keyboard passes completed with evidence; colour-independence and contrast verified on the built UI; findings filed with WCAG references; blocking findings fixed and re-verified; audit report published and linked from the epic; accessibility lead sign-off.

title: Build the speed-of-tape panel (SCR-055) with gauge, strip and z-score
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-001 Speed of tape (Must)**, **US-DET-002 Tape acceleration and threshold alerts (Should)** and **US-DET-003 Book speed (Should)** on **SCR-055 Speed-of-tape panel**: "Rolling trades/sec and notional/sec gauge plus a strip chart, optionally split by side, with a z-score badge used by the rule engine vocabulary (`tape_speed_zscore`)."

The screen contract from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is binding: data from WS `metrics.{symbol}`, windows 1 s / 5 s / 30 s; states calm, elevated, extreme ("threshold chips, **text labels not colour only**") and insufficient sample ("Warming up - 8 s of data"); a11y "The gauge has a text readout ('42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean') as its **primary accessible value**; threshold crossings are announced politely at most once every 5 s; the sparkline has a table alternative"; performance "pushed on `metrics.{symbol}` at 4 Hz; the panel renders at <=4 Hz with a 1 ms budget and **never recomputes z-scores client-side over a long window**".

Design is signed off in E25-D03/D07 (Sprints 11-12), satisfying the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Panel organism for SCR-055 composed of **CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge**, **CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane** (strip-chart mode), **CMP-024 Sparkline**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** (on the book-speed classification only, which US-DET-003 requires to carry it), **CMP-026 EmptyState**.
- Subscription to WS `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics: ["trades_per_sec","volume_per_sec","book_updates_per_sec","tape_acceleration"]` through the shared WS worker; one subscription for the whole family.
- Window selector 1 s / 5 s / 30 s; the active window length is labelled on the panel; changing it resubscribes and the next value is computed on the new window server-side (no client-side re-derivation).
- Per-side split toggle (buy/sell prints per second) rendered as two series with distinct non-colour encodings.
- Z-score badge for `tape_acceleration` with calm / elevated / extreme chips carrying **text labels**, plus the "warming up - N s remaining" state driven by `meta.warming_up_remaining_ms`.
- Book-speed readout with the calm / normal / nervous classification string from the backend, the `(estimated)` badge, and the depth-tier renormalisation annotation on the series (US-DET-003 scenario 2).
- Idle state: an explicit `0` reading when no prints have arrived, never a held last value.
- "Create alert from this threshold" affordance that hands the current metric and threshold to the alert-creation flow (owned by the ALRT epic; this story only launches it with the right payload).
- Table alternative for the strip chart, reachable from the panel header.
- Analytics: `tapespeed.window_changed`, `tapespeed.threshold_changed`, `tapespeed.alert_created`.
- Storybook stories for every documented state.

## Out of scope
The rolling statistics and z-score computation (E25-T01 - backend), alert creation, delivery and cooldown (ALRT epic), the scanner column that reuses `trades_per_sec` (E17/SCR-104), regime (S03), imbalance (S02), detector settings (S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Gauge and strip
  Given a 5 second window
  Then the gauge shows current prints per second and notional per second with units
  And a strip chart shows the recent history
  And the window length is labelled on the panel

Scenario: Window change
  When I switch to a 1 second window
  Then the metric recomputes immediately from the backend on the new window
  And the panel performs no client-side z-score recomputation over a long window

Scenario: Idle market
  Given no prints have arrived for 10 seconds
  Then the gauge reads zero explicitly rather than holding the last value

Scenario: Warming up
  Given the baseline window has insufficient samples
  Then the z-score badge reads warming up with the remaining time, and no z-score value is shown

Scenario: Threshold crossing announced politely
  Given the z-score crosses the configured threshold repeatedly within 5 seconds
  Then at most one polite screen-reader announcement is made in that 5 second period

Scenario: Book speed is labelled estimated
  Then the calm, normal or nervous classification carries the (estimated) badge whose activation opens SCR-058 at the book-speed section

Scenario: Depth tier change
  Given the depth tier changes
  Then the book-speed series shows the renormalisation annotation at that point

Scenario: Render budget
  Given metrics arrive at 4 Hz
  Then the panel renders at most 4 times per second within a 1 millisecond render budget
```

## Technical notes / design
Decode in the shared WS worker and hand the panel a small typed snapshot per tick; do not keep a long history in React state - the strip chart holds a fixed-size Float32Array ring of the displayed window only. Threshold chips are derived from backend-published classification strings; the panel must contain **no numeric threshold constants** (enforced by a lint rule added in this story, per the epic exit criterion "no threshold logic exists in the web client").

Announcements use a polite live region with a 5 s throttle implemented as a leading-edge throttle so the first crossing is announced immediately and subsequent ones are suppressed, rather than delayed.

Number formatting uses the mono numeric token from the CMP-036/CMP-049 token contract; notional is formatted with the symbol's quote currency.

## Test plan
- Unit: window-label rendering; idle-zero rendering; warming-up countdown; throttle emits at most one announcement per 5 s window; renormalisation annotation placement; no threshold constants (lint rule test).
- Component (Storybook + testing-library): each documented state renders its documented copy; window selector resubscribes with the new option; alert affordance dispatches the correct payload.
- E2E (added in E25-Q02): switch window, observe idle-zero on a quiet fixture, open SCR-058 from the estimated badge.
- Perf (E25-Q03): 4 Hz update stream for 10 minutes, assert p95 render <=1 ms and no dropped frames.
- a11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass confirming the text readout is the primary accessible value and the sparkline table alternative is reachable.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public market data, but the subscription requires an authenticated session with `marketdata:read`. Do not render raw backend error payloads in the panel; map to user-facing copy. No secrets in analytics events.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Primary accessible value is the sentence readout ("42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean"). Threshold state is conveyed by text label plus shape, never colour alone. Strip chart has a table alternative. All controls keyboard reachable with visible focus; live region is polite and throttled to one announcement per 5 s.

## Performance notes
Budget: panel render <=1 ms at <=4 Hz (SCR-055). Budget #3 (WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms, hard R2 gate) applies end to end. The panel must not allocate per tick - reuse the ring buffer.

## Observability
Analytics `tapespeed.window_changed`, `tapespeed.threshold_changed`, `tapespeed.alert_created`. Client performance mark around the panel render sampled into the existing frontend performance telemetry.

Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including a frontend code owner; design sign-off from E25-D07 referenced and design QA (E25-D08) passed; Storybook entries for all states; unit and component tests green; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean in CI; QA sign-off on the story group; no open P0/P1.
