title: Build the imbalance tracker panel (SCR-056) with chart cross-highlight
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-004 Imbalance tracker panel (Must)**: "a chart-wide panel listing current imbalance stacks, so that I do not have to hunt for them visually" - each active stack listed with price range, direction, depth, age and status (active/tested/broken); selecting a row scrolls the chart to and highlights the zone; an explicit "no stacks at current thresholds" state links to the thresholds. NFR: "panel updates within 200 ms of a new stack; **fully keyboard navigable**".

**SCR-056** fixes the rest: data from WS `metrics.{symbol}`; "thresholds shared with SCR-032 (single source of truth: changing one prompts to sync the other)"; a11y "Each imbalance event is a row in a **real table** (time, price, ratio, side, stacked count) so the canvas heat strip is never the only representation; the ratio is read as 'bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1'; the stacked-imbalance grouping is stated in text"; performance "bounded 2 000-event ring buffer, renders <=4 Hz with a 1.5 ms budget; recomputation on a threshold change is done backend-side, with a visible recompute state".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Panel for SCR-056 built from **CMP-049 Table** (virtualised, the accessible primary representation), **CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator**, **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard**, **CMP-011 Tag/Chip**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**, **CMP-026 EmptyState**.
- Columns: time, price range, direction (as text plus glyph), stack depth, maximum ratio, age, status (active / tested / broken).
- Incremental updates from `metrics.{symbol}` stack events into a bounded 2 000-entry ring buffer; status transitions update the existing row in place rather than appending a duplicate.
- Row selection scrolls the chart to the bar and highlights the corresponding zone and, where the stack came from footprint cells, links to the originating footprint cell (D03 sign-off item).
- Filters from the screen sketch: "only unfilled" and "alert on new"; the latter hands off to the alert-creation flow owned by the ALRT epic.
- Threshold controls that read and write the **shared** footprint imbalance configuration, with the sync prompt required by SCR-056 when the value differs from SCR-032, and a visible **recompute state** while the backend recomputes.
- Empty state: "no stacks at current thresholds", with a link to the thresholds; stale-data shading.
- Full keyboard navigation: arrow keys move the row cursor, Enter activates (jumps the chart), and the row cursor is announced with the ratio sentence.
- Analytics: `imbalance.threshold_changed`, `imbalance.stacked_min_changed`, `imbalance.event_clicked`, `imbalance.alert_created`.
- Storybook entries for streaming, empty, recomputing, stale and disconnected states.

## Out of scope
Stack detection and lifecycle (E25-T06 - backend), per-cell imbalance computation and the footprint settings dialog SCR-032 (E18), alert delivery (ALRT), chart-side zone rendering primitives (reused from E11/E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Stack list
  Then each active stack is listed with its price range, direction, stack depth, ratio, age and status

Scenario: Navigate to a stack
  When I select a row with the mouse or press Enter on the focused row
  Then the chart scrolls to and highlights the corresponding zone

Scenario: No stacks
  Given no stacks exist at the current thresholds
  Then an explicit no-stacks-at-current-thresholds state is shown with a link to the thresholds

Scenario: Status transition updates in place
  Given a listed active stack becomes tested and then broken
  Then its existing row updates in place and no duplicate row is appended

Scenario: Latency
  Given a new stack is published
  Then it appears in the panel within 200 milliseconds

Scenario: Threshold change is backend-side
  When I change the ratio threshold
  Then a visible recompute state is shown until the backend returns the recomputed stacks
  And the panel performs no client-side recomputation over history
  And I am prompted to sync the value with the footprint settings

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Then every row is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus indicator
  And the focused row is announced including the ratio read as bid 340 versus ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1
  And the direction is conveyed by text, not colour alone
```

## Technical notes / design
The table is the primary representation and the canvas markers are secondary - build the table first and derive the highlight from the selected row, not the reverse. Rows are keyed by the backend's stack key `(bar_ts, price_low, direction)` so in-place updates are trivial and re-emissions cannot duplicate.

Virtualise the list but keep the accessible row semantics intact (`role="row"` on rendered rows with `aria-rowcount` reflecting the full buffer), per the CMP-049 contract.

The threshold control is a view over shared configuration; do not cache a second copy in panel state. On change, show the recompute state until the server confirms - this mirrors SCR-059's "never optimistically" rule.

## Test plan
- Unit: ring-buffer bound at 2 000; in-place status update by key; age formatting; ratio sentence construction; empty/recomputing/stale state selection.
- Component: row activation emits the chart-jump call; threshold change shows recompute state and the sync prompt; `aria-rowcount` reflects the buffer, not the rendered window.
- E2E (E25-Q02): stack appears, click jumps the chart, keyboard path from panel focus to chart highlight.
- Perf (E25-Q03): 4 Hz updates with a full 2 000-entry buffer, p95 render <=1.5 ms; new-stack-to-visible latency <=200 ms.
- a11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass on the table and the ratio announcement.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public market data behind an authenticated session with `marketdata:read`. Threshold writes go through the audited shared-configuration path (never a panel-local endpoint). Bound the ring buffer so a hostile or runaway stream cannot exhaust renderer memory (budget #7).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The event list is a real table and is the primary representation; the canvas heat strip is never the only carrier. Direction and status are text; the ratio is announced in the documented sentence form; stacked grouping is stated in text. Full keyboard navigation is a story NFR, not an enhancement.

## Performance notes
SCR-056 budgets: <=4 Hz render, 1.5 ms per render, bounded 2 000-event ring. Publication-to-visible latency <=200 ms (US-DET-004 NFR). Budget #3 applies end to end; budget #7 (<=1.5 GB renderer) bounds the buffer.

Analytics `imbalance.threshold_changed`, `imbalance.stacked_min_changed`, `imbalance.event_clicked`, `imbalance.alert_created`. Client perf mark around the panel render.

title: Build the market regime panel (SCR-057) with sub-signal breakdown
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-008 Market regime classifier (Must)** on the frontend: "a badge shows the current regime with a confidence value and the sub-signals used (book thickness, realised volatility, tape speed)"; disabling a sub-signal recomputes and the panel "states its composition"; when the lookback cannot be filled "the badge reads 'insufficient data' rather than defaulting to a regime". NFR: "transitions emit events; **(estimated) badge mandatory**".

**SCR-057** fixes the surface: data from WS `metrics.{symbol}` plus `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain?symbol&ts`; "click the badge -> expand the contributing-signal breakdown with each signal's value, threshold and weight"; a11y "the badge is **text-first**; the confidence value is always **numeric**"; performance "pushed at most 1 Hz; the panel renders only on change; the sub-signal breakdown is fetched once per change, not polled. Budget <=1 ms per update."

R9 applies: the panel presents a classification with evidence, never a recommendation. No imperative wording may appear anywhere on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Panel for SCR-057 built from **CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip**, **CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** (mandatory, always visible).
- Badge showing the regime label as text plus the numeric confidence (never a bare colour or bare dots - the dots supplement the number).
- Sub-signal breakdown from `/market/regime/explain`, one row per signal with its value, weight, contribution and direction (supports / opposes / neutral) as text, fetched once per regime change.
- Sub-signal enable/disable control; disabling one triggers a backend recompute and the panel states the composition actually in use.
- Regime-change history strip built from the transition events on `metrics.{symbol}`.
- Insufficient-history state reading "insufficient data" and naming the unfilled lookback - never a defaulted regime.
- "Why this classification?" link opening **SCR-058** at the regime section (E25-S04).
- "Create alert from this regime" affordance handing off to the ALRT flow.
- Analytics: `regime.panel_opened`, `regime.explain_opened`, `regime.sensitivity_changed`, `regime.alert_created`.
- Storybook entries for each regime value, low/high confidence, insufficient data, stale and disconnected.

## Out of scope
Classification, confidence computation and the explain endpoint (E25-T05 - backend), methodology content and the drawer itself (T07 / S04), alert delivery (ALRT), rule DSL binding (E35), ADX/ATR indicator rendering (E17).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Classification with confidence
  Then the badge shows the regime as text with a numeric confidence value
  And the (estimated) badge is present

Scenario: Sub-signal breakdown
  When I activate the badge
  Then each contributing sub-signal is listed with its value, weight, contribution and direction as text

Scenario: Sub-signal disabled
  When I disable tape speed as an input
  Then the classification is recomputed by the backend using the remaining signals
  And the panel states the composition actually used

Scenario: Insufficient data
  Given the lookback cannot be filled
  Then the badge reads insufficient data naming the unfilled lookback
  And no regime value is displayed

Scenario: Render cadence
  Given regime values arrive at most once per second
  Then the panel renders only on change, within a 1 millisecond budget
  And the sub-signal breakdown is fetched once per change, never polled
```

title: Build the detector methodology drawer SCR-058 ("Why estimated?")

## Context
This small story carries a large part of R2's exit criteria. Exit criterion #4: "**Every estimated view carries the (estimated) badge and a popover explaining the heuristic and its failure modes.** A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic." SCR-058 is that explanation: "a drawer opened from any `(estimated)` chip. Explains, per detector, the heuristic used, the inputs, the tunable thresholds, the known false-positive modes, and the hard statement that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed so these are proxies, not ground truth."

It serves **US-DET-009 (Must)** ("every detector documents its method in an info popover; none may render without an (estimated) badge where applicable") and US-CHART-014. Data: `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology` plus current values from `GET /api/v1/detectors/config`. Performance: "opens in <=150 ms and issues no streaming subscriptions."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Drawer for SCR-058 built from **CMP-046 Drawer**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**, **CMP-021 Link**, **CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**.
- One section per estimated signal - iceberg, stop-run, absorption, queue position, order-count footprint, regime, liquidity cluster - each stating: what it infers, from what data, the exact heuristic and **the thresholds currently in force** (merged from `/detectors/config`, not the documented defaults), the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain.
- The sentence "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact" present in every section (a rendering test asserts this).
- Deep-linking: the drawer opens **at the section** for the badge that was activated (`openMethodology(detector)`), from any CMP-227 anywhere in the app.
- A single shared `EstimatedBadge` open-drawer binding so no surface has to wire its own - this is the mechanism that makes the epic's honesty invariant enforceable.
- Links to the detector settings (SCR-059) and to the methodology section of the docs.
- Analytics: `methodology.opened` with `{detector}` (deliberately tracked "so we can tell whether the honesty affordance is actually used").
- Storybook entries per section plus the "config unavailable" degraded state (content still renders; thresholds show as unavailable).

## Out of scope
Authoring the content (E25-T07), the settings dialog (E25-S05), detector implementations, the docs site.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Opens from any estimated badge
  Given any (estimated) badge anywhere in the application
  When I activate it
  Then the methodology drawer opens scrolled to that detector's section

Scenario: Every section is complete
  Then each section states what it infers, from what data, the heuristic, the thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain

Scenario: The honesty sentence
  Then every section contains the sentence that this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact
  And the statement that Bybit provides no L3 or MBO feed is present

Scenario: Thresholds in force, not defaults
  Given the iceberg minimum reload count has been changed from 3 to 5
  Then the iceberg section shows 5

Scenario: Degraded config
  Given GET /detectors/config fails
  Then the content still renders and the thresholds area states that current values are unavailable, with a retry

Scenario: Open latency and no subscriptions
  Then the drawer opens within 150 milliseconds
  And it issues no streaming subscriptions
```

## Technical notes / design
Content is fetched once per session from `/detectors/methodology` and cached; the config overlay is fetched on open. Render content as structured sections from the API rather than hard-coding copy in the client, so T07 remains the single source of the wording.

Focus management per the drawer contract: focus moves to the drawer heading on open, is trapped while open, and returns to the invoking badge on close. The section deep-link must move focus to the section heading, not merely scroll.

## Test plan
- Unit: deep-link resolves each detector id to its section; the required sentence assertion across all sections; config-overlay merge; degraded state.
- Component: opening from a badge in three different host surfaces (SCR-055, SCR-056, SCR-057) all land on the correct section; focus returns to the invoker on close.
- E2E (E25-Q02): open the drawer from the regime badge and from an imbalance row's badge.

- Perf: open <=150 ms measured with the content cache cold and warm; assert no WS subscription is created while open.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Content is public-safe (T07 owns that constraint). The config overlay requires `marketdata:read`; a 403 renders the content without thresholds rather than an error page. No raw backend errors surfaced.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, and this screen carries an extra bar because its purpose is comprehension: plain-language summary first, technical detail second, no jargon without a glossary link (SCR-058 a11y contract). Proper heading hierarchy, focus trap and restore, and the drawer is fully operable by keyboard.

Opens in <=150 ms; content bundled/cached; issues no streaming subscriptions (SCR-058 performance contract).

Analytics `methodology.opened{detector}`. A dashboard panel tracks opens per detector so the team can see whether the honesty affordance is actually used.

title: Build the detector settings dialog SCR-059 with armed-rule warnings
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-009 Detector configuration and audit of estimates (Must)** and the configuration half of US-DET-005/006/007 on **SCR-059 Detector settings dialog**: "Per detector (iceberg, stop-run, absorption, spoof-ish cancellation burst): enable, sensitivity preset (low/medium/high) or explicit thresholds (refill count, window ms, consumed-liquidity ratio, cluster distance ticks), symbol scope, alert routing, and a backtest-on-recorded-history preview showing how many events the current settings would have produced in the last N hours."

Three contract lines govern the behaviour:
- Validation: "thresholds bounded per detector with published ranges; 'Sensitivity high may produce many false positives' warning."
- Performance: "Changes are applied server-side and take effect on the next evaluation window (<=2 s); the dialog shows 'applied' only after the backend confirms, **never optimistically**."
- Audit: "`detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed` with `{detector, key, before, after}` - **audited, because detector output can feed armed rules that place orders**."

US-DET-009 additionally requires per-symbol overrides that persist and are marked as overridden, and a disabled state naming the exact missing dependency with "a one-click action to start recording".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Dialog for SCR-059 from **CMP-043 Dialog**, **CMP-065 FormSection** (one fieldset per detector), **CMP-040 FormField**, **CMP-004 Toggle**, **CMP-008 NumericStepperInput**, **CMP-010 Slider**, **CMP-028 Callout/Banner**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**.
- Per detector: enable toggle, sensitivity preset (low/medium/high) or explicit thresholds, symbol scope (global or this symbol), reset-to-default, current state, **events today**, and its data dependencies (US-DET-009 scenario 1).
- Client-side validation mirroring the published server bounds for immediate feedback, with the server remaining authoritative: iceberg `min_reloads` 2-50, `price_tolerance_ticks` 0-10, `window_ms` 200-60000; stop_run `lookback_bars` 2-500, `penetration_ticks` 1-100, `reversal_pct` 0-100; absorption `min_volume_multiple` 1-50, `max_price_move_ticks` 0-50.
- "Sensitivity high may produce many false positives" warning on the high preset.
- **Armed-rule warning**: before applying a change, list the armed rules that depend on the detector being changed (D04 sign-off item) - this is the control that stops a threshold tweak silently changing live trading behaviour.
- Per-symbol override indication: the panel shows which values are overridden for the current symbol (US-DET-009 scenario 2).
- Missing-dependency state: the detector is shown disabled with the exact missing dependency and a one-click "start recording" action (US-DET-009 scenario 3).
- Non-optimistic apply: an "applying..." state until the backend confirms, then "applied"; on failure the previous values are restored and the error is shown.
- Backtest-on-recorded-history preview: event count the current settings would have produced over the last N hours, with an explicit unavailable state when history is missing.
- Every detector section carries the `(estimated)` badge linking to SCR-058.
- Analytics/audit: `detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed` (audited server-side by E25-T02; the client emits the analytics twin).
- Storybook entries: default, overridden, disabled-missing-dependency, validation error, applying, apply-failed, armed-rule warning.

## Out of scope
Config persistence, bounds enforcement, audit writing and the backtest computation (E25-T02 - backend), methodology content (T07), alert routing destinations (ALRT), the rule engine's own UI (E36/E37), the footprint imbalance thresholds (SCR-032, owned by E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Central panel
  Then every detector lists its parameters, current state, event count today and its data dependencies

Scenario: Per-symbol overrides
  When I set different thresholds for ETHUSDT
  Then they persist per symbol and the panel indicates which values are overridden

Scenario: Dependency missing
  Given a detector requires book history that is not recorded for the symbol
  Then it is shown disabled with the exact missing dependency and a one-click action to start recording

Scenario: Out-of-range value
  When I enter an iceberg minimum reload count of 99
  Then a validation message names the permitted range of 2 to 50 and the change cannot be applied

Scenario: High sensitivity warning
  When I select the high sensitivity preset
  Then a warning states that it may produce many false positives

Scenario: Armed rules are named before applying
  Given an armed rule depends on the stop-run detector
  When I change a stop-run threshold
  Then the dialog lists that rule and requires confirmation before applying

Scenario: Never optimistic
  When I apply a change
  Then the dialog shows applying until the backend confirms, and only then shows applied
  And if the backend rejects the change the previous values are restored with the error shown

Scenario: Estimated framing repeated
  Then each detector section carries the (estimated) badge linking to the methodology drawer
```

## Technical notes / design
Form state is a draft copy; nothing is written until Apply. Bounds constants are **imported from the generated OpenAPI client types**, not retyped, so the dialog cannot drift from the server contract (this is the one permitted place for threshold numbers in the client, and they are generated, not authored).

The armed-rule dependency list is fetched on open from the rule-engine read API (E35) keyed by detector id; when that API is unavailable the dialog states that dependent rules could not be checked and requires an explicit acknowledgement before applying - failing safe, not silent.

Announce the new effective threshold on change (SCR-059 a11y contract) via a polite live region.

## Test plan
- Unit: bounds validation at both ends of every published range; preset-to-threshold mapping; override marking; draft/apply/rollback state machine; armed-rule fetch failure path.
- Component: applying shows applying then applied only after the server responds; a rejected apply restores previous values; the missing-dependency action calls the start-recording endpoint; high-preset warning appears.
- E2E (E25-Q02): change a threshold, confirm the armed-rule warning, apply, and verify the audit record exists (asserted via the admin audit view).
- Security test (E25-X02): a Viewer-role session cannot apply changes; the attempt is rejected and logged.
- a11y: axe-core clean; per-detector fieldsets with units and defaults shown; change announcements verified with a screen reader.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
This dialog is the user-facing half of the epic's highest-value tampering target: detector output can feed armed rules that place orders. Controls: `settings:write` enforced server-side (the dialog is not the gate), server-side bounds enforcement, append-only audit of every change, the armed-rule warning before apply, and fail-safe behaviour when dependent rules cannot be enumerated. The dialog must never disable or bypass a server validation. Reviewed under `security` label in E25-X02.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Per-detector fieldsets with legends; numeric inputs with units and default values shown; each detector has an enable switch and a text description; changing a value announces the new effective threshold politely; validation messages are programmatically associated with their field; the dialog traps focus and restores it on close.

## Performance notes
Apply takes effect within <=2 s (SCR-059). Dialog opens in <=200 ms. The backtest preview is computed backend-side and must not block the dialog - it renders progressively with a loading state.

## Observability
Client analytics `detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed`; the authoritative audit records are written server-side by E25-T02. A dashboard panel shows threshold changes over time alongside detector event rates so a sudden event-rate change can be correlated with a configuration change.

Per section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including a frontend code owner and a security reviewer; design sign-off (E25-D07) and design QA (E25-D08); Storybook entries for all listed states; tests green; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean; security review (E25-X02) closed; QA sign-off.

## Context
US-DET-005 requires that "an absorption marker is **drawn** with its magnitude and an (estimated) badge" and US-DET-007 that "a sweep marker is **drawn** at the extreme with direction and magnitude" and that "parameters are shown in the legend". Those markers live on the chart, not in a panel, and they are rendered by the chart engine's overlay layer rather than by DOM.

The component contract already exists: **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard (iceberg/stop-run/absorption)**, whose a11y note is explicit - "Card (CMP-050) composition with CMP-011 estimated chip **mandatory**". SCR-051 (the DOM/heatmap screen) already shows detector chips with "(estimated)" in its sketch ("detectors: iceberg 63,970 (estimated) - stop-run zone 63,900 (est.)"), so the marker vocabulary must be consistent between the chart and the ladder.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chart overlay layer rendering absorption, iceberg and stop-run events from `metrics.{symbol}` event-like metric points (`MetricPoint.meta`), using the engine's existing marker/annotation primitives from `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` - no new render path.
- Marker encoding: glyph plus text label (direction and magnitude), never colour alone; an `(estimated)` affordance on every marker opening SCR-058 at that detector's section.
- **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard** on hover/focus of a marker showing detector, time, price, direction, magnitude, and the **parameter snapshot in force when it fired** (the `params_snapshot` from the event) - this is the "see *why* it fired" inspector the roadmap scope line requires.
- Legend entry naming the active detectors and their current parameters (US-DET-007 scenario "Parameters").
- Stop-run breakout annotation rendered distinctly when enabled (US-DET-007 scenario "No reversion").
- Keyboard access: markers are reachable in the chart's DOM-mirror accessibility tree (the same mechanism used for footprint cells and DOM rows, roadmap section 6.4 a11y gate), with the card content announced.
- Clamped marker density: above a configured events-per-viewport threshold, markers cluster with a count badge rather than overplotting.
- Feature-flag awareness: when a detector's flag is off or it is disabled for a missing dependency, no markers render and the legend states why.
- Storybook/engine-demo entries for each marker type and the clustered state.

## Out of scope
Detector computation (T03/T04), the methodology drawer itself (S04), settings (S05), the DOM ladder's own detector chips (E21 renders them, consuming the same events), alerting (ALRT), journal auto-tagging.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Absorption marker
  Given an absorption event is published
  Then a marker is drawn at its price and time with its magnitude and an (estimated) affordance

Scenario: Sweep marker
  Given a stop-run event is published
  Then a marker is drawn at the swept extreme with direction and magnitude
  And the legend shows the active detection parameters

Scenario: Why it fired
  When I hover or focus a marker
  Then a DetectorEventCard shows the detector, time, price, direction, magnitude and the parameter snapshot in force when it fired

Scenario: No reversion
  Given a penetration that did not revert and breakout annotations are enabled
  Then a distinct breakout annotation is drawn, visually distinguishable from a sweep marker without relying on colour

Scenario: Density clamp
  Given more detector events than the per-viewport threshold
  Then markers cluster with a count badge rather than overplotting
  And the frame budget is not exceeded

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Then markers are reachable through the chart DOM mirror and their card content is announced

Scenario: Detector disabled
  Given a detector is disabled by its feature flag or a missing dependency
  Then no markers for it render and the legend states the reason
```

## Technical notes / design
Reuse the engine's instanced-marker primitive; a detector marker is a glyph instance plus a text label subject to the same text-LOD rule the footprint uses (hide glyph text below the per-cell pixel-width threshold proven in E06/E18) so the marker layer cannot be the thing that breaks budget #1.

Events are appended to a bounded per-viewport buffer; on pan/zoom the visible window is recomputed from the buffer rather than refetched. Clustering is computed in screen space at layout time, not in data space, so it stays stable under zoom.

The card is DOM (CMP-134) positioned against the marker's screen coordinates, not drawn in WebGL, so its text is selectable and accessible.

## Test plan
- Unit: marker-to-screen placement; clustering threshold behaviour; params-snapshot rendering; disabled-detector legend copy; text-LOD suppression.
- Component: hover and keyboard focus both open the card with identical content; the estimated affordance opens SCR-058 at the right section.
- E2E (E25-Q02): markers appear on a recorded fixture; focusing one via keyboard announces the card.
- Perf (E25-Q03): full R2 scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD pane) **plus** the detector marker layer at the worst-case event density, p95 frame time <=16.6 ms and never below 30 fps (budgets #1 and #2, R2 exit criterion 2).
- a11y: axe-core on the card; DOM-mirror reachability test.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public market data. Markers must always carry the estimated affordance - a marker that looks like exchange-provided fact is the failure mode this epic exists to prevent. No raw backend payloads rendered in the card.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Markers are distinguishable by glyph and text, not colour alone (roadmap a11y gate: colour-blind-safe palettes; non-colour encodings). Markers reachable and announced via the chart DOM mirror, matching the footprint-cell and DOM-row treatment. The card is real DOM with selectable text.

## Performance notes
Budgets #1 (p95 <=16.6 ms with the full scene) and #2 (never below 30 fps worst case), both hard gates. The marker layer's own budget is <=0.5 ms per frame at nominal density; the density clamp exists to hold it.

## Observability
Client metric for markers rendered per frame and clustering activations; analytics `detector.marker_opened{detector}`.

## Definition of Done
Per section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including the chart-engine code owner; design sign-off (E25-D07) and design QA (E25-D08); engine benchmark added to the CI perf suite and passing budgets #1/#2 with the marker layer enabled; Storybook/engine-demo entries; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean; QA sign-off.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T03 and E25-T04 (the events to render) and E25-D07 (design handoff). Relies on the E11 chart-engine marker and DOM-mirror primitives and on the E25-S04 badge binding.

title: Build MetricsEngine: rolling tape and book statistics with z-scores
body:
## Context
Every DET surface reads from one backend engine. US-DET-001 (Speed of tape, Must), US-DET-002 (Tape acceleration, Should) and US-DET-003 (Book speed, Should) are all *rolling statistics over the normalised trade and book streams*, and their screen contracts (SCR-055) state explicitly: "Rolling statistics are computed backend-side and pushed on `metrics.{symbol}` at 4 Hz; the panel renders at <=4 Hz with a 1 ms budget and **never recomputes z-scores client-side over a long window**."

`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` fixes the transport: one topic `metrics.{symbol}`, options `metrics[]`, `bar_type`, `param`, per-metric `params`, default throttle 250 ms, no binary frame. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` fixes the vocabulary: `tape_speed` (`window_ms=1000`, exact), `tape_speed_zscore` (`fast_ms=1000`, `base_ms=300000`, alert `>3.0`, exact). The OpenAPI description of `/market/metrics` names the codes as `trades_per_sec` / `volume_per_sec` / `book_updates_per_sec` (windows 1 s / 5 s / 30 s) and `tape_acceleration` (1 s vs 300 s baseline, alert >3x).

This task creates the engine and the publishing path that T02-T06 then plug detectors into.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/metrics_engine.py` (module M9): a per-symbol `MetricsEngine` consuming the normalised `publicTrade` stream and the reconstructed book deltas from E21, maintaining ring buffers for the 1 s / 5 s / 30 s windows and a 300 s baseline.
- Metric codes produced here: `trades_per_sec`, `volume_per_sec` (notional per second), `book_updates_per_sec`, `tape_acceleration` (z-score of fast window vs baseline), `imbalance_ratio` passthrough, plus the book-derived `book_imbalance`, `book_thickness`, `spread_ticks`, `realized_vol_1m`, `atr_14`.
- Per-side split of tape speed (buy/sell prints per second) as required by SCR-055 ("optionally split by side").
- Publication on WS `metrics.{symbol}` honouring `metrics[]` selection and `throttle_ms` (default 250 ms), in the `MetricsUpdate` frame shape defined in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 14.7, with `estimated` set per metric from the vocabulary.
- REST backfill via `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` for these codes, returning `MetricSeries` with `params` echo and `unit` (`ratio`, `index`, `base_volume`).
- Persistence at the fixed 1 s cadence into QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` columns `trades_per_sec`, `notional_per_sec`, `book_imbalance`, `book_thickness`, `spread_ticks`, `realized_vol_1m`, `atr_14` (DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol)).
- Explicit zero on idle: with no prints in the window the value is `0`, never the last value (US-DET-001 scenario "Idle market").
- "Warming up" semantics: while the baseline window has fewer than `min_samples` the z-score series emits `null` with `meta.warming_up_remaining_ms` (US-DET-002 scenario "Baseline too short").
- Depth-tier renormalisation: when the subscribed book depth tier changes, `book_updates_per_sec` is renormalised and a `meta.renormalised_at` marker is emitted on the series (US-DET-003 scenario "Depth-tier dependence").
- Prometheus counters/histograms listed under Observability.

## Out of scope
Detector heuristics (T02-T04), regime classification (T05), imbalance stacks (T06), any UI, the calm/normal/nervous *labelling* thresholds' presentation (the engine emits the classification string; the panel renders it), alert dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tape speed and notional
  Given a stream of publicTrade messages for BTCUSDT
  When the 5 second window is requested
  Then trades_per_sec and volume_per_sec are published at 4 Hz on metrics.BTCUSDT
  And each series carries its window length in params

Scenario: Window change recomputes immediately
  Given a subscription with window 5s
  When the client resubscribes with window 1s
  Then the next published value is computed over the 1 second window, not a decayed 5 second value
  And the effective window is echoed in the subscribe acknowledgement

Scenario: Idle market reads zero
  Given no prints have arrived for 10 seconds
  Then trades_per_sec publishes 0 explicitly rather than holding the last value

Scenario: Warming up
  Given the 300 second baseline has fewer than the minimum samples
  Then tape_acceleration publishes null with the remaining warm-up time in meta
  And no z-score is published until the baseline is filled

Scenario: Depth tier change
  Given the book subscription changes from depth 200 to depth 50
  Then book_updates_per_sec is renormalised and the series carries a renormalisation marker at that timestamp

Scenario: One subscription carries the family
  Given a client subscribes to metrics.BTCUSDT with metrics ["trades_per_sec","book_updates_per_sec","tape_acceleration"]
  Then all three arrive on one subscription within the throttle interval
```

## Technical notes / design
Ring buffers are fixed-size arrays of (timestamp, value) indexed by a monotonic counter, not deques of Python objects, to hold budget #8. Maintain incremental sums so a window read is O(1): on each event push and evict expired entries by timestamp; recompute the sum by add/subtract rather than re-summing. The baseline keeps Welford running mean/variance over 1 s buckets so the z-score is `(fast - mean) / stdev` with `stdev` floored to avoid division blow-ups in dead markets; when `stdev` is below the floor the z-score publishes `null` rather than a huge number.

Clock-agnostic by construction: the engine takes timestamps from the event, never from `time.time()`, so E26 replay drives it unchanged. This is a hard review item - a `time.time()` call in this module is a defect.

Interface sketch:

```python
class MetricsEngine:
    def on_trade(self, ev: TradeEvent) -> None: ...
    def on_book_delta(self, ev: BookDeltaEvent) -> None: ...
    def sample(self, ts_ms: int) -> list[MetricSample]: ...  # called on the publish tick
```

`MetricSample` carries `metric`, `value`, `unit`, `estimated`, `params`, `meta`. Publishing is done by the existing WS fan-out; the engine never touches sockets.

Config keys: `orderflow.metrics.publish_hz` (default 4), `orderflow.metrics.persist_hz` (1), `orderflow.metrics.baseline_ms` (300000), `orderflow.metrics.min_baseline_samples` (60).

## Test plan
- Unit: window eviction at boundaries; O(1) incremental sum equals a naive re-sum over 10 000 random events; idle-window zero; z-score against a hand-computed fixture; stdev floor produces null; warming-up countdown; renormalisation marker on tier change; per-side split sums to the total.
- Property test: for random event streams, `trades_per_sec` over window W equals `count(events in [t-W, t]) / W` within float tolerance.
- Determinism: the same fixture replayed twice yields identical sample streams (feeds E25-Q03).
- Contract: WS `metrics.{symbol}` frames validate against `cv://ws/v1/metrics.schema.json`; REST responses validate against `MetricsResponse`.
- Integration: recorded BTCUSDT fixture covering normal session, volatility burst and a WS disconnect/resync.
- Perf: 2 000 trades/s plus 100 ms book cadence sustained for 10 minutes within budget #11.
- Coverage >=85 % on the module.

## Security notes
Public market data, but the subscription is session-gated and requires `marketdata:read` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` x-rbac on `/market/metrics`). Guard against resource exhaustion: cap `metrics[]` at 12 entries (OpenAPI `maxItems: 12`), reject unknown metric codes with a 4xx rather than silently ignoring, and bound the REST backfill range so a single request cannot scan an unbounded window (DoS, STRIDE-D in E25-X01).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). The engine must emit the calm/normal/nervous classification as a *string*, so the client never has to derive a label from a colour.

## Performance notes
Budget #6: engine sample-to-outbound-frame <=20 ms p95. Budget #3: end-to-end WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms with this metric set added (hard R2 gate, measured in E25-Q03). Budget #11: <=0.5 vCPU per symbol for all of M9 combined; this engine's share is targeted at <=0.1 vCPU. Budget #8: ring buffers sized so per-symbol metric state stays under 20 MB.

## Observability
`orderflow_metrics_publish_lag_seconds` (histogram), `orderflow_metrics_events_consumed_total{kind}`, `orderflow_metrics_window_evictions_total`, `orderflow_metrics_warming_up{symbol,metric}` (gauge). Log at INFO on depth-tier renormalisation with before/after tiers.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 4.2: code merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; unit/contract/integration tests green; coverage >=85 %; metric vocabulary section of `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` updated if any code or default changed; Prometheus metrics registered and a Grafana panel added; no `time.time()` in the module (checked by a lint rule).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E08 (normalised `publicTrade` stream and the in-process bus) and E21 (reconstructed L2 book deltas and depth-tier notifications). Consumed by T02-T06 and every E25 story.

## Branch
`feat/detectors-metrics-engine`. PR size guidance: split into (1) engine + unit tests, (2) WS/REST wiring + contract tests, (3) persistence.

title: Detector framework, config persistence and the three detector endpoints
body:
## Context
US-DET-009 (Must) requires "one place to configure all detectors and see their assumptions", with per-symbol overrides, an explicit disabled state naming a missing data dependency, and an info popover documenting each method. SCR-059's analytics/audit section is unambiguous about why this is not ordinary settings plumbing: "`detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed` with `{detector, key, before, after}` - **audited**, because detector output can feed armed rules that place orders."

The API surface already exists in the contract: `GET|PUT /api/v1/detectors/config` (`DetectorConfig`, `settings:write` scope `self` for PUT, `marketdata:read` for GET), `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology` (`DetectorMethodology[]`), `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain` (`RegimeExplanation`). This task builds the framework those endpoints sit on: a `DetectorRegistry`, a uniform `Detector` interface, the `DetectorEvent` bus that alerts/rules/journal later consume, and config storage with global and per-symbol layers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/detectors/base.py`: `Detector` protocol - `id`, `estimated: bool`, `required_inputs: list[str]`, `on_trade`, `on_book_delta`, `on_bar_close`, `configure(params)`, emitting `DetectorEvent(detector, symbol, ts_ms, price, direction, magnitude, confidence, estimated, params_snapshot, meta)`.
- `server/orderflow/detectors/registry.py`: registration, per-symbol instantiation, feature-flag gating on `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector`, `metrics.absorption` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` feature-flag table, all default `false`), and dependency checking (a detector whose `required_inputs` are not being recorded for the symbol is reported `disabled_missing_dependency` with the exact missing input name).
- `DetectorEvent` publication onto the shared in-process event bus and onto `metrics.{symbol}` as event-like metric points (`MetricPoint.meta` carries "per-point detail for event-like metrics (iceberg, stop_run, absorption)" per the OpenAPI schema), plus persistence of the score columns `iceberg_score`, `stoprun_score`, `absorption_score` in `orderflow_metrics`.
- Config storage in Postgres: a global `DetectorConfig` row plus per-symbol override rows; effective config = global merged with symbol override; the response marks which keys are overridden.
- Endpoint implementations: `GET /detectors/config`, `PUT /detectors/config` (validates against the published bounds: iceberg `min_reloads` 2-50, `price_tolerance_ticks` 0-10, `window_ms` 200-60000; stop_run `lookback_bars` 2-500, `penetration_ticks` 1-100, `reversal_pct` 0-100; absorption `min_volume_multiple` 1-50, `max_price_move_ticks` 0-50; exhaustion `min_delta_divergence` >=0), `GET /detectors/methodology` (content supplied by T07).
- Audit: every enable/threshold change writes an append-only audit record per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 8 with `{actor, detector, key, before, after, symbol_scope}`.
- Apply semantics required by SCR-059: "Changes are applied server-side and take effect on the next evaluation window (<=2 s); the dialog shows 'applied' only after the backend confirms, never optimistically" - so PUT returns only once the registry has re-configured live instances.
- Dependency-check endpoint data: the `GET /detectors/config` response includes, per detector, `state` (`enabled` / `disabled` / `disabled_missing_dependency`), the missing input, and `events_today` for the SCR-059 and SCR-058 displays.

## Out of scope
The individual heuristics (T03, T04), regime (T05), imbalance stacks (T06), methodology *content* (T07), the UI (S05), alert routing and cooldown (ALRT domain), rule-engine binding (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Effective config with per-symbol override
  Given a global iceberg min_reloads of 3
  And an ETHUSDT override of 5
  When GET /api/v1/detectors/config is requested for ETHUSDT
  Then min_reloads is 5 and the response marks that key as overridden

Scenario: Bounds enforced
  When PUT /api/v1/detectors/config sets iceberg.min_reloads to 99
  Then the request is rejected with a validation error naming the permitted range 2 to 50
  And no audit record of a change is written

Scenario: Change is audited and confirmed only after it takes effect
  When an authorised user changes stop_run.reversal_pct from 60 to 45
  Then an append-only audit record is written with detector, key, before, after and actor
  And the response returns only after the live detector instances have been reconfigured
  And the new value is in force within 2 seconds

Scenario: Missing dependency
  Given BTCUSDT has no recorded L2 book history
  Then the iceberg detector reports state disabled_missing_dependency naming the missing input
  And it emits no events

Scenario: Feature flag off
  Given the feature flag metrics.iceberg_detector is false
  Then no iceberg detector instance is created and the config endpoint reports the detector as disabled with the flag as the reason

Scenario: Unauthorised change
  Given a Viewer-role session
  When PUT /api/v1/detectors/config is called
  Then the request is rejected with 403 and the attempt is logged
```

## Technical notes / design
The registry owns lifecycle, not the detectors: detectors are pure state machines fed by the engine loop, which makes replay (E26) free - the same instances are driven by replayed events. Reconfiguration replaces the params snapshot on the next evaluation boundary, never mid-window, so an event can always be attributed to exactly one parameter set (`params_snapshot` on every `DetectorEvent` exists for this reason and is what SCR-058 renders as "thresholds in force").

Postgres tables: `detector_config(scope, symbol, detector, params_json, updated_at, updated_by)` with `scope in ('global','symbol')` and a unique key on `(scope, symbol, detector)`. Audit rows go to the existing append-only audit table; no update or delete path exists.

Error codes: `DETECTOR_UNKNOWN`, `DETECTOR_PARAM_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `DETECTOR_DEPENDENCY_MISSING`, `DETECTOR_DISABLED_BY_FLAG`.

## Test plan
- Unit: config merge precedence; every published bound rejected at both ends and accepted at the boundary; audit record shape; dependency resolution; flag gating; params_snapshot immutability within a window.
- Contract: `/detectors/config` GET and PUT against the OpenAPI schema (round-trip PUT then GET returns exactly what was set); `/detectors/methodology` shape.
- Integration: change a threshold, assert the next event carries the new `params_snapshot` and that it took <=2 s.
- Security: RBAC matrix test - Viewer 403, Manager/Owner per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7; audit written on every accepted change and on every rejected attempt.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
This is the highest-value tampering target in the epic: detector thresholds feed armed rules that place orders (STRIDE-T, STRIDE-R in E25-X01). Controls: `settings:write` on PUT, append-only audit with actor identity, published bounds enforced server-side (never trust the dialog), no mass-assignment (`additionalProperties: false` on `DetectorConfig` is enforced, unknown keys rejected), and a rate limit on PUT to prevent audit-log flooding. Data classification: configuration = internal; market data = public.

## Accessibility notes

## Performance notes
Config reads are cached in-process and invalidated on write; the read path must not hit Postgres per evaluation. Budget #13: `/detectors/config` GET p95 <150 ms, PUT p95 <300 ms backend-internal. Detector dispatch overhead (registry loop, excluding heuristic work) <=5 microseconds per event.

title: Implement absorption and iceberg detectors (estimated) in M9
body:
## Context
Implements the backend of **US-DET-005 Absorption detector (Must)** - "aggression fails to move price ... an absorption marker is drawn with its magnitude and an (estimated) badge", NFR: "detection is deterministic given the same inputs, validated against recorded fixtures in CI" - and **US-DET-006 Iceberg / hidden-order detector (Should)** - "a level is consumed and refilled at least N times within the window ... flagged with the refill count and an (estimated) badge", NFR: "never used as the sole trigger for an automated live action unless the user explicitly acknowledges the estimate".

Bybit's public feed is anonymous and aggregated and exposes no L3/MBO data, so iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences, not observations. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` makes `confidence="estimated"` mandatory for every heuristic and states plainly that "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface that shows one of these values must render CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the detector methodology drawer. US-DET-006's third scenario is a product requirement, not a nicety: "the info popover states plainly that Bybit exposes no L3/MBO data and this is an L2-derived inference".

Parameters come from `DetectorConfig` as published, refined by the E25-K01 calibration report.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/detectors/absorption.py`: aggressive volume at a price over the evaluation window exceeding `min_volume_multiple` times the rolling median while the price advance stays within `max_price_move_ticks`; emits `DetectorEvent(detector="absorption", magnitude=absorbed_volume, direction=side_absorbed, estimated=True)`.
- `server/orderflow/detectors/iceberg.py`: per-price resting-size tracking from book deltas; a reload is counted when size at a price is consumed below a fraction of its prior resting size and returns within `price_tolerance_ticks` and the size tolerance inside `window_ms`; a candidate is flagged at `min_reloads`; emits `magnitude=reload_count` and `meta.executed_volume` (the `iceberg_executed_volume` metric of `24-internal-schemas.md`).
- Metric codes published on `metrics.{symbol}`: `absorption`, `iceberg` (both `estimated: true`), with per-event detail in `MetricPoint.meta`.
- Score persistence into `orderflow_metrics.absorption_score` and `.iceberg_score`.
- Recompute over the loaded range on a threshold change (US-DET-005 scenario "Thresholds"), driven server-side with a visible recompute state - the client never recomputes.
- Bounded per-price state with an eviction policy (levels untouched for `window_ms * k` are dropped) so memory holds under budget #8.
- Golden-fixture test data committed for the CI determinism gate.

## Out of scope
Stop-run (T04), regime (T05), chart markers and the event card UI (S06), settings UI (S05), methodology copy (T07), alerting (ALRT), the exhaustion detector (config surface exists, but exhaustion is delivered with the footprint/divergence work in E18/E23).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Absorption flagged
  Given aggressive volume at a price exceeds min_volume_multiple times the rolling median
  And the price advance stays within max_price_move_ticks
  Then an absorption event is emitted with its magnitude, the absorbed side and estimated true

Scenario: Threshold change recomputes
  When the absorption volume threshold or price tolerance is changed
  Then detection is recomputed server-side over the loaded range
  And the recompute is observable as a state, not as a silent gap

Scenario: Iceberg replenishment
  Given a price level is consumed and refilled at least min_reloads times within window_ms
  Then an iceberg candidate is emitted with the refill count and estimated true

Scenario: False-positive control
  When min_reloads is raised
  Then strictly fewer or equal candidates are flagged over the same fixture
  And the active parameters are present in the event's params snapshot

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the same recorded fixture is replayed twice
  Then the emitted absorption and iceberg event streams are byte-identical

Scenario: Never silently exact
  Then every absorption and iceberg point published on metrics.{symbol} has estimated set to true
```

## Technical notes / design
Both detectors are pure state machines over `(TradeEvent | BookDeltaEvent)` with no wall-clock access, so replay drives them unchanged. The iceberg tracker keeps a small per-price record `(last_size, peak_size, reloads, first_seen_ms, last_reload_ms, executed_volume)` in a dict keyed by integer tick index, capped at the subscribed depth plus a margin; eviction is a periodic sweep at the evaluation boundary, not per event.

Absorption's rolling median is computed over a fixed-size window of per-price aggressive volumes using a two-heap structure so the update is O(log n); the median rather than the mean is deliberate - a single block print must not define "normal".

Cooldown: each detector suppresses repeat events at the same price within its own window and counts suppressions, so a level that keeps reloading yields one event with a growing reload count rather than a stream.

Determinism rules (enforced in review): no `time.time()`, no `set`/`dict` iteration order dependence in output ordering (sort emissions by `(ts_ms, price, detector)`), no floating-point accumulation across the whole session - window sums are rebuilt at the window boundary.

## Test plan
- Unit: absorption triggers exactly at the threshold and not one tick below; price-move tolerance boundary; median window; iceberg reload counting with and without the tick tolerance; eviction does not lose an in-flight candidate; cooldown suppression counting; monotonicity property - raising `min_reloads` never increases the event count on a fixed fixture.
- Golden fixture: one recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day with a committed expected event stream; any drift fails CI (roadmap section 6.4 "Correctness" gate).
- Determinism: double-run equality (roadmap section 6.4 "Determinism" gate; also exercised by E25-Q03).
- Integration: fixtures for normal session, high-volatility burst and thin book; assert event rates land within the bands recommended by E25-K01.
- Perf: microbenchmark per trade and per book delta; combined detector cost within the M9 share of budget #11.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Detector output can feed armed rules (E35). US-DET-006's NFR is a hard control: the event carries `estimated=True` and `requires_acknowledgement=True` so the rule engine can refuse to arm a live action on it alone without explicit user acknowledgement. Resource exhaustion: per-price state is bounded and the recompute path is range-limited and rate-limited (STRIDE-D). No PII.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). Events carry a text `direction` and a numeric `magnitude` so the UI never needs colour alone.

## Performance notes
Budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU per symbol, whole of M9) and budget #8 (<=300 MB per symbol) - the per-price iceberg state is the memory risk and must be measured, with the measured figure recorded on the ticket. Evaluation must add <=2 ms p95 to the engine tick so budget #6 (<=20 ms fan-out add-on) holds.

## Observability
`orderflow_detector_events_total{detector="absorption"|"iceberg",symbol}`, `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector}`, `orderflow_detector_suppressed_total{detector,reason="cooldown"}`, `orderflow_iceberg_tracked_levels{symbol}` (gauge). INFO log on recompute start/finish with the range and the resulting event delta.

Per section 4.2 of the DoR/DoD: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; golden fixture and determinism tests in CI; coverage >=85 %; K01's recommended defaults applied (or the deviation justified in the PR); `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` metric-vocabulary rows confirmed accurate; feature flags remain default-off until E25-Q03 signs off the calibration.

title: Implement stop-run / liquidity-sweep detector (estimated) in M9
body:
## Context
Implements the backend of **US-DET-007 Stop-run / liquidity sweep detector (Must)**: "Given price breaks a marked swing extreme, trades through resting liquidity above the threshold and reverts within the window, Then a sweep marker is drawn at the extreme with direction and magnitude". Its NFR binds it to three consumers: "events feed the alert engine, the rule DSL and journal auto-tags". Its declared dependencies are US-DOM-002 (book depth, delivered by E21) and US-IND-005 (swing/structure detection) - the story is explicit that the sweep is measured against *marked swing extremes*, and `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` elsewhere insists a divergence "is only drawn once both swings are confirmed by the swing detector, never on provisional swings". The same discipline applies here.

Parameters as published in `DetectorConfig`: `lookback_bars` (2-500, default 20), `penetration_ticks` (1-100, default 2), `reversal_pct` (0-100, default 60), refined by E25-K01.

Bybit's public feed is anonymous and aggregated and exposes no L3/MBO data, so iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences, not observations. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` makes `confidence="estimated"` mandatory for every heuristic and states plainly that "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface that shows one of these values must render CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the detector methodology drawer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/detectors/stop_run.py`: maintains confirmed swing highs/lows over `lookback_bars`; on penetration beyond a confirmed extreme by `penetration_ticks`, opens a candidate recording the liquidity consumed above/below the extreme; confirms a sweep when price retraces `reversal_pct` of the penetration excursion within the reversion window; emits `DetectorEvent(detector="stop_run", price=extreme, direction, magnitude=liquidity_consumed, estimated=True, meta={penetration_ticks, reversion_ms, reversal_pct_achieved})`.
- Explicit **no-sweep** outcome: a penetration that does not revert within the window closes the candidate with no event, and optionally emits a distinct `breakout` annotation when the `breakout_annotations` option is enabled (US-DET-007 scenario "No reversion").
- Metric code `stop_run` on `metrics.{symbol}` with `estimated: true`; score persisted to `orderflow_metrics.stoprun_score`.
- Recompute over the loaded range on a parameter change, with the active parameters exposed for the legend (US-DET-007 scenario "Parameters").
- Golden-fixture test data committed for the determinism gate.

## Out of scope
Absorption/iceberg (T03), regime (T05), the chart marker rendering and legend (S06), settings UI (S05), alert delivery, journal auto-tagging (journal epic), the swing/structure detection algorithm itself (consumed from the indicator engine, US-IND-005).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sweep detected
  Given price breaks a confirmed swing extreme by at least penetration_ticks
  And trades through resting liquidity above the configured threshold
  And reverts by at least reversal_pct of the excursion within the reversion window
  Then a stop_run event is emitted at the extreme with direction, magnitude and estimated true

Scenario: No reversion is not a sweep
  Given price breaks the extreme and does not revert within the window
  Then no stop_run event is emitted
  And when breakout annotations are enabled a distinct breakout annotation is emitted instead

Scenario: Provisional swings are never used
  Given a swing extreme that the swing detector has not yet confirmed
  Then no candidate is opened against it

Scenario: Parameters change
  When reversion window or the liquidity threshold is changed
  Then detection recomputes server-side over the loaded range
  And the events carry the new parameter snapshot

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the same recorded fixture is replayed twice
  Then the emitted stop_run event streams are identical
```

## Technical notes / design
Candidate state is one small record per active extreme: `(extreme_price, side, opened_ts, peak_excursion_ticks, liquidity_consumed, deadline_ts)`. Liquidity consumed is accumulated from trades beyond the extreme, using the aggressor side that Bybit publishes directly - no tick-rule inference is needed or permitted. Deadlines are evaluated at the engine tick, driven by event timestamps, not by a timer, so replay is exact.

Only confirmed swings open candidates; when the swing detector later revises structure, already-emitted events are not retracted (events are immutable history) but the recompute path regenerates them for the loaded range, which is why the UI must render from the recomputed stream rather than accumulating locally.

Ordering: emissions are sorted by `(ts_ms, price)` before publication so double-run equality holds.

## Test plan
- Unit: penetration exactly at and one tick below the threshold; reversal exactly at `reversal_pct`; deadline boundary (reversion on the last millisecond counts, one millisecond later does not); provisional-swing rejection; breakout annotation on/off; liquidity accumulation uses feed-provided aggressor side.
- Golden fixture: recorded symbol-day with a committed expected stop_run stream; drift fails CI.
- Determinism: double-run equality.
- Integration: high-volatility burst fixture (the sweep-rich case) and thin-book fixture (the false-positive-rich case); event rates within the bands from E25-K01.
- Perf: microbenchmark per trade; combined M9 detector cost within budget #11.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Stop-run events feed the rule DSL and can therefore participate in armed actions; the event carries `estimated=True` and the acknowledgement flag defined in T03 so a heuristic can never silently become the sole trigger of a live order. Recompute is range- and rate-limited (STRIDE-D). No PII.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). `direction` is emitted as text (`sweep_high` / `sweep_low`) and `magnitude` numerically, so S06 never needs colour alone.

## Performance notes
Evaluation adds <=1 ms p95 to the engine tick; candidate state is O(active extremes), bounded by `lookback_bars`. Budgets #6, #8, #11 as per the epic.

## Observability
`orderflow_detector_events_total{detector="stop_run",symbol}`, `orderflow_stop_run_candidates_open{symbol}` (gauge), `orderflow_stop_run_expired_total` (penetrations that never reverted), `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector="stop_run"}`.

title: Implement market-regime classifier and /market/regime/explain
body:
## Context
Implements the backend of **US-DET-008 Market regime classifier (Must)**: "a badge shows the current regime with a confidence value and the sub-signals used (book thickness, realised volatility, tape speed)"; disabling a sub-signal recomputes the classification "using the remaining signals and states its composition"; and when the lookback cannot be filled "the badge reads 'insufficient data' rather than defaulting to a regime". NFR: "classification exposed as `regime` to the rule DSL; transitions emit events; (estimated) badge mandatory."

The contract is already fixed. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` defines `RegimeExplanation` with `regime` in `[trending_up, trending_down, ranging, volatile_expansion, compression]`, `confidence` 0-1, `as_of`, and `signals[]` each with `name`, `value`, `weight`, `contribution`, `direction` in `[supports, opposes, neutral]` - "so the regime badge is explainable rather than an opaque verdict". `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` names the composition: `market_regime` = enum from **ADX + Hurst + ATR%**, confidence basis **estimated**; and the OpenAPI `/market/metrics` description lists `adx` (14), `atr` (14), `hurst` (R/S window 256), `regime` (combined ADX/Hurst classification). QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` stores `regime` (SYMBOL, 'trend_up'|'trend_down'|'range'|'volatile'|'calm') and `regime_confidence`.

R9 applies: a regime badge must read as a *classification with evidence*, never as a recommendation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/regime.py`: computes `adx(14)`, `atr(14)`, `hurst` (R/S, window 256), `realized_vol_1m`, plus the order-flow sub-signals `book_thickness` and `trades_per_sec` from E25-T01 and CVD slope from E23; combines them into the published enum with a confidence in 0-1 and a per-signal contribution.
- Sub-signal enable/disable: the classifier accepts a signal mask; disabling a signal reweights the remainder and the response states the composition actually used (US-DET-008 scenario 2).
- Insufficient-data state: when any required lookback is unfilled, the classifier publishes `regime = null` with `meta.reason = "insufficient_data"` and the missing lookback named - never a default regime.
- Publication on `metrics.{symbol}` as the `regime` metric at **at most 1 Hz** (SCR-057 performance section), `estimated: true`; persistence into `orderflow_metrics.regime` and `.regime_confidence` at the 1 s cadence; enum mapping between the API enum and the QuestDB SYMBOL values documented in one place.
- **Transition events**: a change of classification emits a `DetectorEvent(detector="regime", meta={from, to, confidence})` onto the shared bus, which is what the SCR-057 transition strip and the rule DSL consume.
- `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain?symbol` returning `RegimeExplanation` computed from the same evaluation that produced the current badge - the explanation must never be recomputed independently, or badge and explanation could disagree.
- Hysteresis so the badge does not flicker between regimes on a boundary value, with the hysteresis band documented and exposed in the explanation.

## Out of scope
The panel UI (E25-S03), methodology copy (T07), the ADX/ATR indicator *rendering* (E17 indicators), CVD computation (E23), rule DSL binding (E35), any ML classifier (explicitly out of R2 scope), OI-trend sub-signal beyond what E24 already publishes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Classification with evidence
  Given sufficient history for all enabled sub-signals
  Then the regime metric publishes one of trending_up, trending_down, ranging, volatile_expansion, compression
  And a numeric confidence between 0 and 1
  And GET /market/regime/explain returns each sub-signal with its value, weight, contribution and direction

Scenario: Sub-signal disabled
  When tape speed is disabled as an input
  Then the classification is recomputed from the remaining signals
  And the explanation states the composition actually used

Scenario: Insufficient data
  Given the Hurst lookback of 256 samples cannot be filled
  Then the regime publishes null with reason insufficient_data naming the unfilled lookback
  And no regime enum value is published

Scenario: Transition emits an event
  Given the classification changes from ranging to trending_up
  Then a regime transition event is emitted with from, to and confidence

Scenario: Badge and explanation agree
  When the explain endpoint is called immediately after a published regime value
  Then it returns the same regime, confidence and as_of timestamp as the published value

Scenario: Always estimated
  Then the regime metric is published with estimated true
```

## Technical notes / design
One evaluation produces one immutable `RegimeVerdict(as_of, regime, confidence, signals[], composition, hysteresis_band)`; the WS publisher and the explain endpoint both read that object from a per-symbol cache. This is the only way to satisfy "badge and explanation agree" and it also makes the explain endpoint free (SCR-057: "the sub-signal breakdown is fetched once per change, not polled").

Confidence is the normalised margin between the winning class score and the runner-up, clamped to 0-1, so it is interpretable rather than arbitrary; the definition is written into the methodology content (T07) verbatim.

Hurst via rescaled range over a 256-sample window using incremental partial sums; ADX and ATR reuse the existing indicator implementations from the indicator engine rather than being re-implemented here - a second ADX would be a correctness hazard. Evaluation is driven by event timestamps (clock-agnostic) for replay parity.

Config keys: `orderflow.regime.publish_hz` (1), `orderflow.regime.hurst_window` (256), `orderflow.regime.adx_period` (14), `orderflow.regime.atr_period` (14), `orderflow.regime.hysteresis` (default 0.05 of the score margin).

## Test plan
- Unit: each sub-signal against hand-computed fixtures; Hurst against a known fractional-Brownian series; classification boundaries; hysteresis prevents flapping on a synthetic boundary-oscillating series; confidence in 0-1; insufficient-data path for each lookback; signal-mask reweighting sums to 1.
- Contract: `RegimeExplanation` validates against the OpenAPI schema; the enum values are exactly the five published ones.
- Consistency test: published regime equals `/market/regime/explain` for 1 000 consecutive evaluations.
- Integration: trending, ranging and volatile recorded fixtures each classify as expected for the majority of their duration.
- Determinism: double-run equality on a recorded fixture.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Read-only public market data behind `marketdata:read`. R9 advice boundary is the real control: the API returns a classification and its evidence, never an instruction; no field named `signal`, `recommendation` or `action` may appear in this response. Explain is cached per symbol, so it cannot be used to force expensive recomputation (STRIDE-D).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend) - but the classifier must emit a text enum and a numeric confidence (never a colour or a bare score) so SCR-057 can be text-first as its catalogue entry requires.

## Performance notes
SCR-057: classification computed backend-side and pushed at most 1 Hz; panel budget <=1 ms per update. Evaluation cost <=3 ms per second per symbol. Budgets #6, #11 as per the epic.

## Observability
`regime_transitions_total{symbol,from,to}`, `regime_confidence` (gauge per symbol), `regime_insufficient_data{symbol}` (gauge), `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector="regime"}`. INFO log per transition with the contributing signals.

Per section 4.2: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; contract test against `RegimeExplanation`; enum mapping to the QuestDB `regime` SYMBOL values documented in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 4.11; coverage >=85 %; the confidence definition written into the methodology content ticket (T07); consistency test in CI.

title: Track stacked imbalance runs over footprint cells and publish them
body:
## Context
Backend for **US-DET-004 Imbalance tracker panel (Must)**: "each active stack is listed with price range, direction, depth, age and status (active/tested/broken)". NFR: "panel updates within 200 ms of a new stack". Declared dependency: US-FP-008 (stacked imbalances in the footprint, E18).

The division of labour matters. E18 computes per-cell diagonal/horizontal imbalance flags with a configurable ratio (roadmap section 6.2: "imbalance detection with configurable ratio and diagonal/horizontal modes"). E25 turns those per-bar flags into **stacks that live over time** and tracks whether price has since traded back through them. SCR-056 states the thresholds are "shared with SCR-032 (single source of truth: changing one prompts to sync the other)" and that "recomputation on a threshold change is done backend-side, with a visible recompute state rather than a client-side full-history pass".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/imbalance_stacks.py`: consumes footprint cell imbalance flags from E18; groups `>= min_stack` consecutive same-direction imbalanced price levels within a bar into a stack with `price_low`, `price_high`, `direction`, `depth`, `ratio_max`, `created_ts`.
- Lifecycle: `active` -> `tested` (price returns into the zone) -> `broken` (price trades fully through it); status transitions emitted as events so the panel updates incrementally rather than re-fetching.
- Publication as the `imbalance_ratio` / stack metric points on `metrics.{symbol}` with per-stack detail in `MetricPoint.meta`; counts persisted to `orderflow_metrics.stacked_imbalance_up` and `.stacked_imbalance_down`.
- Threshold source-of-truth: read the ratio and `min_stack` from the same configuration E18 uses (`price_grouping`, `imbalance_ratio`, `min_stack` are already `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` options); no second copy of these numbers.
- Server-side recompute over the loaded range on a threshold change, with an observable recompute state.
- Bounded retention: at most 2 000 stacks per symbol in the publishable ring (matching SCR-056's 2 000-event client ring buffer), older ones available via REST backfill.

## Out of scope
The per-cell imbalance ratio computation (E18), the panel UI (E25-S02), footprint rendering, alerting on new stacks (ALRT), the settings dialog control (E25-S05 / E18's footprint settings dialog SCR-032).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Stack formed
  Given three consecutive price levels in a bar are imbalanced in the same direction above the configured ratio
  And min_stack is 3
  Then one stack is published with its price range, direction, depth, maximum ratio and creation time

Scenario: Lifecycle
  Given an active stack
  When price returns into its price range
  Then its status becomes tested
  And when price trades fully through it the status becomes broken
  And each transition is published as an incremental update

Scenario: Latency
  Given a new stack forms
  Then it is published within 200 milliseconds of the bar update that created it

Scenario: Threshold change
  When the imbalance ratio or minimum stack depth is changed
  Then stacks are recomputed server-side over the loaded range and a recompute state is published
  And the client performs no full-history recomputation

Scenario: Single source of truth
  Then the ratio and minimum stack depth used here are read from the same configuration the footprint engine uses, with no second stored copy
```

## Technical notes / design
Stacks are keyed by `(bar_ts, price_low, direction)` so a re-emission after a bar revision replaces rather than duplicates. Lifecycle evaluation runs on trade events against the open-stack list, which is small (bounded by the visible/loaded range), so an O(n) scan per trade is acceptable at R2 volumes; if profiling says otherwise, index open stacks in a sorted price array and binary-search the traded price.

"Traded through" means price has printed beyond the far edge of the zone, not merely touched it - the distinction is the difference between `tested` and `broken` and must be stated in the methodology content (T07).

## Test plan
- Unit: grouping at exactly `min_stack` and at `min_stack - 1`; non-consecutive levels do not group; direction mixing breaks a stack; tested/broken transitions at the exact boundary price; re-emission after bar revision replaces by key; ring bound at 2 000.
- Integration: recorded fixture; stack counts match an independent DuckDB recomputation over the Parquet tier (roadmap section 6.3 exit criterion 6 pattern).
- Latency: new stack published within 200 ms of the bar update (measured in CI with a synthetic feed).
- Determinism: double-run equality.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Public data behind `marketdata:read`. The recompute path is range-limited and rate-limited (STRIDE-D). Thresholds are shared configuration - changing them is audited through the same path as the footprint settings, so there is exactly one audited write path.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend) - the published stack carries `direction` as text ("buy"/"sell") and explicit `bid_volume`/`ask_volume` numbers, because SCR-056 requires the ratio to be announced as "bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1".

## Performance notes
SCR-056: panel renders <=4 Hz with a 1.5 ms budget; publication within 200 ms of stack formation. Backend evaluation <=1 ms per bar update. Budgets #6, #8 as per the epic.
