title: Author detector methodology content, vocabulary docs and feature flags
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion #4 is a content requirement as much as an engineering one: "Every estimated view carries the (estimated) badge **and a popover explaining the heuristic and its failure modes**. A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic." SCR-058's sign-off checklist demands, per estimated signal, "what it infers, from what data, the exact heuristic and thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain", and that "the words 'this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact' appear in each section".

The API schema `DetectorMethodology` requires `detector`, `inputs`, `assumption`, `false_positive_modes` (and optional `display_name`, `confidence_basis`) for each of `iceberg, stop_run, absorption, exhaustion, big_trade, regime`. This ticket writes that content - sourced from the E25-K01 calibration report and the shipped implementations - and lands the feature-flag configuration that keeps the heuristics off until they are trusted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Methodology content for every enum value of `DetectorMethodology.detector`, served by `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology`, stored as versioned content in the repo (not in the database) so it is reviewed like code.
- For `big_trade` and `exhaustion`, coordinate the wording with E22 and E18 respectively rather than writing a competing description - one methodology entry per signal, app-wide.
- The `confidence_basis` string for `regime` stating exactly how confidence is computed (the normalised margin definition from E25-T05).
- Update the metric-vocabulary tables in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` so every DET metric code, its default params and its `exact`/`estimated` confidence are accurate against the shipped code.
- Feature flags `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector`, `metrics.absorption` documented with their rollout criterion ("on only after E25-Q03 signs off the calibration") and wired so flipping a flag is audited (`config.changed`, `SYSTEM_CONFIG_EDIT`).
- A short ADR **only if** K01 concluded that a published `DetectorConfig` default must change; otherwise a note in the epic recording that the defaults were confirmed.
- Copy review by the design/content owner so SCR-058's plain-language-first requirement is met.

## Out of scope
The drawer UI (E25-S04), the settings UI (E25-S05), detector implementations, translation/localisation (single-locale app), marketing copy.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every estimated signal is documented
  When GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology is called
  Then it returns an entry for each of iceberg, stop_run, absorption, exhaustion, big_trade and regime
  And each entry has inputs, an assumption stated plainly, and at least two false-positive modes

Scenario: The honesty sentence is present
  Then each entry states that Bybit exposes no L3 or MBO data and that the value is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact

Scenario: Thresholds in force are shown
  Given the detector configuration has been changed from the defaults
  Then the drawer content combined with GET /detectors/config shows the values actually in force, not the documented defaults

Scenario: Vocabulary matches the code
  Then every DET metric code in docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md matches the code's registered metrics and its estimated flag, verified by an automated test

Scenario: Flags default off
  Then metrics.iceberg_detector, metrics.stop_run_detector and metrics.absorption default to false, and flipping any of them writes an audit record
```

## Technical notes / design
Content lives in `server/orderflow/methodology/*.md` with front-matter mapping to the schema fields; a loader validates at startup that every registered detector has a methodology entry and fails fast otherwise. That startup assertion is what makes "no estimated surface without an explanation" enforceable rather than aspirational.

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the detector subsystem
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and the R2 roadmap schedules "STRIDE R2 epics [S10-S13]". E25 looks like a read-only analytics feature and is not: **detector output can feed armed rules that place orders** (SCR-059's audit rationale, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` rule-action vocabulary), and detector thresholds are user-writable. That turns a market-data view into part of the trading control path, which is why the threat model must be done before E25-T02 builds the configuration write path.

Scheduled Sprint 10, ahead of the Sprint-12 implementation it constrains.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE analysis across the epic's trust boundaries (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 4): browser to API, API to M9 engines, M9 to QuestDB/Postgres, and the detector-event bus to the rule engine.
- Per category, with concrete threats and named controls:
  - **Spoofing**: unauthenticated or cross-session subscription to `metrics.{symbol}`; session fixation on the settings dialog.
  - **Tampering**: modifying detector thresholds to change armed-rule behaviour; bypassing published bounds by calling the API directly; mass-assignment via unexpected keys on `DetectorConfig`; altering methodology content to misrepresent an estimate as fact.
  - **Repudiation**: a threshold change with no attributable actor; an armed rule firing on a detector event with no record of the parameters in force (mitigated by `params_snapshot` on every event).
  - **Information disclosure**: minimal (market data is public) - but verify error responses do not leak internal table names, file paths or exchange credentials, and that recorded-history availability does not leak other users' recording configuration.
  - **Denial of service**: unbounded `metrics[]` selection; oversized REST backfill ranges; repeated `recompute` requests; unbounded per-price iceberg state; subscription amplification across many symbols.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a Viewer changing detector configuration; a detector-driven rule action escaping the acknowledgement requirement of US-DET-006's NFR.
- **Abuse cases** written as testable scenarios and handed to E25-Q01 for inclusion in the test plan.
- A control list mapped to the implementing tickets (T02 bounds/RBAC/audit, T01 caps, T03/T04 acknowledgement flag and state bounds, S05 armed-rule warning).
- Risk ratings and accepted residual risks, signed by the security engineer and the architect.
- SAST/DAST rule additions where the analysis identifies a pattern worth automating (for example a Semgrep rule forbidding threshold constants in the web client, and a ZAP scan of the detector endpoints).

## Out of scope
Implementation of the controls (the named tickets), pen-testing (scheduled before R4 live enablement), the rule engine's own threat model (E35), the recorder's (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six STRIDE categories covered
  Then each category has at least one concrete threat for this epic, or a documented justification for why it does not apply

Scenario: Every threat has a control and an owner
  Then each identified threat maps to a named control and the ticket that implements it

Scenario: The armed-rule path is analysed
  Then the model explicitly analyses the path from a detector event to an armed rule action
  And names the controls that prevent a heuristic being the sole trigger of a live order without acknowledgement

Scenario: Abuse cases handed over
  Then at least four abuse cases are written as testable scenarios and accepted into the E25-Q01 test plan

Scenario: Automation identified
  Then any pattern worth automating is raised as a SAST or DAST rule with its rationale

Scenario: Signed off
  Then the model is reviewed and signed by the security engineer and the architect before E25-T02 begins
```

## Technical notes / design
Model the data flow concretely: `Bybit WS -> ingestion (M4) -> book/tape (M9) -> MetricsEngine -> DetectorRegistry -> DetectorEvent bus -> {WS fan-out, orderflow_metrics, alert engine, rule engine}` plus the control flow `browser -> PUT /detectors/config -> config store -> registry reconfigure`. The interesting boundary is the second one: it is a low-privilege-looking settings write that reaches into the trading control path.

Name the acknowledgement control precisely: `DetectorEvent.estimated` plus the requires-acknowledgement flag, honoured by the rule engine at arming time, is what implements US-DET-006's NFR. Without it the NFR is only a sentence.

## Test plan
Abuse cases become test cases in E25-Q01 and, where automatable, in E25-Q02 (unauthorised change) and E25-Q03 (DoS caps under load). The threat model itself is reviewed, not tested.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security work. Data classification: public market data; internal configuration; audit records are security-relevant and append-only. Review label required on E25-T02 and E25-S05.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - except the recommendation, carried into D04/S05, that security-relevant confirmations must be operable by keyboard and screen reader.

## Performance notes
DoS controls interact with budgets: caps must be set high enough not to break legitimate use (12 metrics per subscription is already the OpenAPI cap) and low enough to bound cost within budgets #8 and #11.

## Observability
Specify the security-relevant events to emit: `detector.threshold_changed`, `detector.enabled_changed`, rejected-change attempts with actor and reason, and rate-limit trips on the recompute endpoints.

STRIDE model documented in the security space and linked from the epic; threats rated with controls and owning tickets; abuse cases accepted into E25-Q01; SAST/DAST rules raised; residual risks accepted in writing; signed by the security engineer and the architect; completed before E25-T02 starts (it is a `blocked_by` of that ticket).

title: Security review of the detector config write path and event bus
body:
## Context
Verification counterpart to E25-X01: a white-box review of the implemented controls on the two paths that matter - the detector configuration write path (browser -> `PUT /api/v1/detectors/config` -> config store -> live registry) and the detector event bus (detector -> event -> alert/rule engine), where a heuristic can reach an armed trading action.

`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a security review per feature alongside SAST/SCA/DAST. R2's security quality gate names E21 and E26 explicitly for STRIDE, but E25's write path is the one that touches trading behaviour, so it gets a dedicated review.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Code review of `PUT /detectors/config`: authentication, `settings:write` authorisation with scope, server-side bounds enforcement for every published range, rejection of unknown keys (`additionalProperties: false`), no mass assignment, rate limiting, and idempotent behaviour under retry.
- Verification that **every** accepted and rejected change writes an append-only audit record with actor, detector, key, before, after and symbol scope, and that the record cannot be updated or deleted.
- Verification that `DetectorEvent.estimated` and the acknowledgement flag are set on every heuristic event and are honoured at rule-arming time, satisfying US-DET-006's NFR ("never used as the sole trigger for an automated live action unless the user explicitly acknowledges the estimate").
- Verification of the DoS controls: `metrics[]` cap, REST backfill range bound, recompute rate limit, bounded per-price iceberg state and bounded event buffers.
- Verification that the SCR-059 armed-rule warning cannot be bypassed by calling the API directly - i.e. that the warning is a UX affordance over a server-side control, not the control itself; if it is the only control, that is a finding.
- RBAC test evidence: Viewer rejected, Manager/Owner per the RBAC matrix (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7).
- DAST (ZAP) scan of `/detectors/*` and `/market/metrics` and `/market/regime/explain`; SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) findings triaged for the epic's modules; dependency scan for any new packages.
- Confirmation that error responses leak no internal detail.
- Findings filed with severity; all high and critical fixed before sign-off; residual risks accepted in writing.

## Out of scope
The threat model (E25-X01), penetration testing (pre-R4), the rule engine's internals (E35 has its own review), infrastructure hardening.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Authorisation is enforced server-side
  Given a Viewer-role session
  When PUT /api/v1/detectors/config is called directly, bypassing the UI
  Then the request is rejected with 403 and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Bounds cannot be bypassed
  When the API is called directly with values outside every published range
  Then each is rejected server-side with a validation error
  And no configuration change occurs

Scenario: Unknown keys rejected
  When the request body contains a key not present in DetectorConfig
  Then the request is rejected rather than the key being ignored

Scenario: Audit is complete and immutable
  Then every accepted and rejected change produces an append-only audit record containing actor, detector, key, before, after and scope
  And no code path updates or deletes those records

Scenario: Heuristics cannot silently arm a live action
  Given a rule armed on a detector event
  Then arming requires the explicit acknowledgement recorded for estimated detectors
  And the event carries its parameter snapshot for later attribution

Scenario: DoS caps hold
  Then the metrics selection cap, backfill range bound and recompute rate limit are enforced and return errors rather than degrading the service

Scenario: Scans clean
  Then DAST on the detector endpoints and SAST on the epic's modules produce no unresolved high or critical findings
```

## Technical notes / design
Attempt the bypasses directly against the API with a scripted client rather than through the UI; a control that only exists in the dialog is the specific failure this review is designed to catch, and it is an easy one to ship.

Check idempotency and races: two concurrent PUTs must not interleave into a mixed configuration, and the registry reconfigure must be atomic at an evaluation boundary (which is also a correctness property, per E25-T02).

## Test plan
Review plus targeted tests: RBAC matrix tests, direct-API bypass attempts, bounds fuzzing across every published range, concurrent-PUT race test, audit-immutability test, and the ZAP/Semgrep/Bandit runs. Tests that encode controls are merged into the permanent suite rather than run once.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security work. Data classification: configuration (internal), audit (security-relevant, append-only), market data (public). Findings of high or critical severity block E25-Q05 sign-off and therefore the R2 PRR.

## Accessibility notes
Confirm the armed-rule confirmation and validation messaging remain operable by keyboard and screen reader after any security-driven change.

## Performance notes
Confirm rate limits and caps are set so legitimate use is unaffected; measure the config read path's in-process caching so authorisation and validation do not add per-evaluation cost.

## Observability
Verify that rejected attempts, rate-limit trips and configuration changes are all observable (logs, metrics, audit) and that an operator could reconstruct who changed what and when, and which parameters were in force when a given detector event fired.

## Definition of Done
Review completed with findings filed; all high and critical findings fixed and re-verified; control tests merged into the permanent suite; DAST and SAST clean or triaged with written acceptance; RBAC evidence attached; residual risks accepted; security engineer sign-off recorded; result reported into E25-Q05 and the R2 PRR.
